title: html lang is hardcoded to "vi" and never updates when the user switches to English
description: app/layout.tsx:17 renders <html lang="vi"> statically. The i18n provider's setLang (lib/i18n.tsx:215-218) only updates React state and localStorage; nothing ever writes document.documentElement.lang. When the user switches to English via the LanguageSwitcher, every page renders English text under lang="vi", so screen readers (VoiceOver, NVDA, TalkBack) select a Vietnamese TTS voice and mispronounce all English content — a WCAG 3.1.1/3.1.2 (Language of Page/Parts) failure. This app is explicitly bilingual per requirements.md §2 and targets seniors, a population with higher assistive-tech usage.
proposal: In I18nProvider, sync the document language: add `useEffect(() => { document.documentElement.lang = lang; }, [lang])` (covers both the localStorage restore on mount and subsequent switches). Keep lang="vi" as the SSR default in app/layout.tsx since Vietnamese is the default locale.
verifierNote: app/layout.tsx:17 renders static <html lang="vi">; lib/i18n.tsx:215-218 setLang only calls setLangState + localStorage.setItem, and grep confirms zero writes to document.documentElement anywhere. App is explicitly bilingual (requirements.md:8 'Vietnamese (default) + English, user-switchable'), so English UI renders under lang="vi". Proposal (useEffect syncing documentElement.lang, keep vi SSR default) is correct and minimal.

title: Modal has no dialog semantics, no focus management, no focus trap, and no Escape/keyboard close
description: Modal (components/ui.tsx:135-161) renders a plain fixed-position div: no role="dialog", no aria-modal="true", no aria-labelledby pointing at the h3 title (line 156). When it opens (contacts connect form, app/dashboard/contacts/page.tsx:86; Wi-Fi change, app/dashboard/device/page.tsx:162) focus stays on the triggering button behind the overlay — a screen reader user gets no indication a dialog opened. Tab freely moves into the obscured background content (header, tabs, other cards) since nothing is inert. The only dismissal besides Cancel is a mouse-only backdrop onClick (line 150); there is no Escape handler, and focus is not restored to the trigger on close. Fails WCAG 2.4.3 (Focus Order), 4.1.2 (Name/Role/Value), and the ARIA dialog pattern.
proposal: Give the inner container role="dialog", aria-modal="true", and aria-labelledby={titleId} (generate with useId). On open, move focus to the dialog (or its first field) via a ref + useEffect; on close, return focus to the previously focused element. Add a keydown handler for Escape calling onClose, and trap Tab within the dialog (or render via <dialog>.showModal(), which provides role, focus trap, and Escape for free).
verifierNote: components/ui.tsx:135-161: Modal is a plain div — no role/aria-modal/aria-labelledby (title h3 at ui.tsx:156), no focus move, no focus trap, no Escape handler; only dismissal besides Cancel is the backdrop onClick at ui.tsx:150. Used at app/dashboard/contacts/page.tsx:86 and app/dashboard/device/page.tsx:162. Grep shows the only ARIA in the codebase is Logo.tsx:12-13. Proposal follows the standard dialog pattern; high is justified.

title: Async status/error messages (Alert) are never announced — no role="alert" or aria-live anywhere
description: Alert (components/ui.tsx:114-133) renders a plain div with color classes. It is the sole mechanism for every dynamically-appearing async outcome in the app: sign-in/sign-up/forgot-password errors (app/sign-in/page.tsx:33, app/sign-up/page.tsx:42, app/forgot-password/page.tsx:35,45), connect errors inside the contacts modal (app/dashboard/contacts/page.tsx:92), mic-denied and "sample submitted" messages (app/dashboard/voice-training/page.tsx:133-142), and Wi-Fi errors/success (app/dashboard/device/page.tsx:77-81,168). Because these appear after an async operation with no role="alert"/aria-live and no focus movement, a screen reader user who submits the sign-in form with wrong credentials hears nothing — the button just reverts to "Đăng nhập" and the failure is silent. Fails WCAG 4.1.3 (Status Messages). A grep confirms zero aria-live/role="alert"/role="status" occurrences in the codebase.
proposal: In Alert, add role="alert" for kind="error" and role="status" (polite) for kind="success". Because role="alert" on a newly-mounted node is announced reliably in React, this single component change fixes all nine call sites. For form submission errors, additionally consider moving focus to the alert (tabIndex={-1} + ref.focus()) so low-vision magnifier users also land on it.
verifierNote: components/ui.tsx:114-133: Alert is a plain styled div. Grep over app/, components/, lib/ finds no aria-live/role="alert"/role="status" (only role="img" in Logo.tsx:12). All cited call sites verified: sign-in/page.tsx:33, sign-up/page.tsx:42, forgot-password/page.tsx:35,45, contacts/page.tsx:92, voice-training/page.tsx:135,140, device/page.tsx:79,168. Sign-in failure path (sign-in/page.tsx:24-27) only setError+setBusy(false), so the button label reverts silently as claimed. Single-component fix at the sole status mechanism is high-leverage; confirmed at high.

title: Voice recording flow: state changes are silent to screen readers and focus is dropped when control buttons unmount
description: The record controls (app/dashboard/voice-training/page.tsx:149-182) fully swap per recState: clicking "Ghi âm" unmounts the Record button (150-159) and mounts Stop (160-170); clicking Stop unmounts it and mounts audio/re-record/submit (171-181). Each transition destroys the currently-focused button, so keyboard focus falls back to <body> and the user must Tab from the page top to find Stop — while the mic is live. The "Đang ghi âm…" indicator (165-169) is a plain span with a color-pulse dot, not in a live region, so a blind user gets no confirmation that recording started — the microphone can be recording without them knowing. Similarly, sample history badges flip pending→processed via 5s polling (41-45, 192-207) with no announcement. Fails WCAG 2.4.3 (Focus Order) and 4.1.3 (Status Messages) on the app's core flow (requirements.md §4 Tab 2).
proposal: 1) Wrap the recording status area in an aria-live="assertive" region so "Recording…" is announced on start. 2) On state transition, move focus to the newly relevant control (ref.focus() on Stop after start; on the audio player or Re-record after stop). Alternatively keep one toggle button whose label/pressed state changes (aria-pressed) so it never unmounts. 3) Add a polite live region (visually hidden is fine) announcing when a pending sample becomes processed/failed during polling.
verifierNote: app/dashboard/voice-training/page.tsx:150-181: the three recState branches fully mount/unmount their buttons, so the focused Record/Stop button is destroyed on each transition; the 'recording' indicator at 165-169 is a plain span with an animate-pulse dot, no live region. Polling flips badge status silently (41-45, 192-207). This is the core flow (requirements.md Tab 2) with a live mic while focus is dropped to body — high is appropriate; proposal (live region + focus management or a persistent toggle) is sound.

title: Disconnect is destructive but fires immediately with no confirmation
description: The Disconnect button (app/dashboard/contacts/page.tsx:74) calls `disconnect(ch)` directly onClick, which immediately POSTs `/api/contacts/:id/disconnect` (page.tsx:46-49). There is no confirmation step, while connecting requires re-entering all credentials from scratch (the form starts empty, page.tsx:25 `setCreds({})`). One stray click on a card button — in a product aimed at seniors (i18n tagline 'Người bạn đồng hành AI cho người lớn tuổi') — severs the channel and forces the user to hunt down their OA ID / access token again. A destructive action next to the primary action with zero friction is a data-loss-adjacent trap.
proposal: Reuse the existing Modal component for a confirm dialog ('Ngắt kết nối {name}? Bạn sẽ cần nhập lại thông tin xác thực để kết nối lại.') with a danger-variant confirm button (Button already supports variant="danger", components/ui.tsx:20). Only call ContactsAPI.disconnect on confirm.
verifierNote: app/dashboard/contacts/page.tsx:74 `onClick={() => disconnect(ch)}` fires disconnect() (page.tsx:46-49) with no confirmation; openConnect resets creds to {} (page.tsx:25) so reconnecting requires re-entering all tokens. Modal exists (components/ui.tsx:135-161) and Button supports variant="danger" (ui.tsx:20), so the proposal fits existing patterns. The seniors tagline is real (lib/i18n.tsx:10). Since credentials are not stored client-side and a non-technical user may not have the OA ID/token at hand, an accidental disconnect is effectively unrecoverable without help — high stands.

title: disconnect() has no error handling or double-submit protection — rejected promise is unhandled and user gets zero feedback
description: `disconnect` (app/dashboard/contacts/page.tsx:46-49) does `await ContactsAPI.disconnect(ch.id); load();` with no try/catch and no busy flag. (1) If the POST fails (network down, 401 from expired token, 404), the rejection escapes the async onClick handler as an unhandled promise rejection — the UI shows nothing, the badge stays 'Đã kết nối', and the user cannot tell whether anything happened. (2) The button is never disabled during the request, so rapid clicks fire multiple concurrent POSTs and refetches; the page-level `busy` state (page.tsx:16) is only used inside the connect modal. Contrast with `connect` (page.tsx:30-44) which handles both correctly.
proposal: Wrap in try/catch and surface failure via a page-level Alert or toast; track an in-flight channel id (e.g. `const [pendingId, setPendingId] = useState<string|null>(null)`) and render the Disconnect button with `disabled={pendingId === ch.id}` plus a spinner/label swap, mirroring the connect button's `busy ? t("loading") : ...` pattern (page.tsx:112).
verifierNote: disconnect (page.tsx:46-49) is exactly `await ContactsAPI.disconnect(ch.id); load();` — no try/catch, and the Disconnect button (page.tsx:74) has no disabled prop, so rapid clicks fire concurrent POSTs. `busy` (page.tsx:16) is only set inside connect (page.tsx:33,42) and only read by the modal submit button (page.tsx:111-112). ApiError from lib/api.ts:43 would escape the onClick as an unhandled rejection with zero UI feedback, in contrast to connect's catch (page.tsx:39-40). Proposal mirrors existing patterns; sound.

title: Failed contacts fetch is swallowed into an empty list — error indistinguishable from 'no channels', and no empty state exists
description: `load` does `ContactsAPI.list().then(setChannels).catch(() => setChannels([]))` (app/dashboard/contacts/page.tsx:18-20). Any fetch failure (offline, 401, 500) silently produces `channels = []`, which renders just the title/description over an empty grid (page.tsx:60-84) — no error message, no retry, and also no explicit empty-state copy if the list is genuinely empty. Worse, `load()` is re-run after every connect/disconnect mutation (page.tsx:38,48), so a successful disconnect followed by a failed refetch wipes the entire visible channel list even though the server state is fine.
proposal: Track a load error state separately: on catch, keep the previous `channels` value if one exists and show an Alert with a retry button; on first-load failure show an error panel instead of an empty grid. Add an explicit empty-state message for a genuinely empty list. Alternatively (or additionally) patch locally from the mutation response — both endpoints return `{ id, connected }` (lib/be.ts:52,58) — so a refetch failure can never erase already-known channels.
verifierNote: page.tsx:18-20 is exactly `.then(setChannels).catch(() => setChannels([]))`; load() is re-run after mutations at page.tsx:38 and :48, so a failed refetch after a successful disconnect replaces known channels with []. The grid (page.tsx:60-84) has no empty-state or error branch — a fetch failure renders title/desc over nothing, indistinguishable from zero channels. Both endpoints do return {id, connected} (lib/be.ts:52,58), so local patching is viable. Claim and proposal both sound.

title: No toast/feedback primitive — mutation success/error is communicated inconsistently or not at all
description: The only feedback primitive is the inline Alert (components/ui.tsx:114-133); there is no toast/snackbar, so every page invents its own mutation feedback and several mutations have none: (1) contacts disconnect (app/dashboard/contacts/page.tsx:46-49) has no busy state, no success message, and no catch — a failed disconnect is an unhandled rejection with zero UI feedback; (2) contacts connect success just closes the modal silently (contacts/page.tsx:36-38); (3) voice sample submit (app/dashboard/voice-training/page.tsx:103-114) uses try/finally with no catch — a failed upload shows nothing and the recording is wiped by reset() only on success, but the user gets no error either way; success shows a persistent inline Alert (voice-training/page.tsx:138-142); (4) device Wi-Fi success sets `updated` (app/dashboard/device/page.tsx:48,77-81) which is never cleared, so the 'Wi-Fi updated' banner persists for the rest of the session even after unrelated refreshes. Users cannot tell whether some actions worked, and stale success banners misinform.
proposal: Add a Toast primitive + ToastProvider (success/error kinds, auto-dismiss ~4s, aria-live polite) in components/ui.tsx and app/providers.tsx. Route all mutation outcomes through it: connect/disconnect success+failure, voice submit success+failure, Wi-Fi update success. Keep inline Alert only for form-validation errors inside modals/auth forms. Clear or auto-dismiss the device `updated` state.
verifierNote: All four claims check out: Alert (components/ui.tsx:114-133) is the only feedback primitive; contacts disconnect (app/dashboard/contacts/page.tsx:46-49) is `await ContactsAPI.disconnect(ch.id); load();` with no busy/catch/success UI — a rejected promise is unhandled with zero feedback; connect success silently closes the modal (contacts/page.tsx:36-38); voice submit (voice-training/page.tsx:103-114) is try/finally with no catch, setSuccess/reset only run on success (106-110) so a failure shows nothing; device `updated` is set at device/page.tsx:48 and never set back to false anywhere (grep confirms only lines 33/48 touch it), so the success banner (77-81) persists for the page's lifetime including manual Refresh (72-74). Silent mutation failure for an elderly-targeted product justifies high; the toast proposal is a standard, fitting fix.

title: No focus-visible styles in any primitive; logs select removes the outline entirely
description: Button's base classes (components/ui.tsx:26) define no focus-visible ring, so buttons fall back to the browser default outline while Input replaces it with a brand ring (ui.tsx:59 `outline-none ... focus:ring-2 focus:ring-sen-light`) — two different focus appearances. Worse, the hand-rolled select on the logs page (app/dashboard/logs/page.tsx:37-38) copies `outline-none` but replaces it with only `focus:border-sen` (a subtle 1px border color change, no ring), leaving keyboard focus nearly invisible. Tab links (app/dashboard/layout.tsx:74-87), the sign-out icon button (layout.tsx:61-67), LanguageSwitcher buttons (components/LanguageSwitcher.tsx:10-21), and log row expanders (logs/page.tsx:84-87) all rely on inconsistent browser defaults. For a product aimed at elderly users, keyboard/switch navigation has no coherent focus system.
proposal: Define one focus token — e.g. `focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-sen` (or ring equivalent) — and bake it into Button, Input, and a new Select primitive; apply the same utility to tab links, LanguageSwitcher, and icon buttons. Remove `outline-none` from the logs select or pair it with the ring.

Tab links (dashboard/layout.tsx:74-87), sign-out button (61-67), LanguageSwitcher buttons (LanguageSwitcher.tsx:10-21), and log expanders (logs/page.tsx:84-87) have zero focus classes (grep for 'focus' across app/components finds only ui.tsx:59 and logs/page.tsx:38). Tailwind 4 preflight keeps browser default outlines, so the 'inconsistent defaults' framing is accurate. High is fair for the a11y dimension of this product.

title: Backend error messages surface raw English text to Vietnamese-default UI
description: All user-visible error paths bypass the i18n dictionary. lib/api.ts:40-43 throws ApiError with either the server's `error` string or the hardcoded English template `Request failed (${res.status})`. Every mock route returns English-only strings — 'Invalid credentials' (app/api/auth/sign-in/route.ts:8), 'Invalid email' and 'Password must be at least 6 characters' (app/api/auth/sign-up/route.ts:7,11), 'Failed to connect' (app/api/device/wifi/route.ts:7), and the interpolated 'Invalid credentials: missing oaId, accessToken' (app/api/contacts/[id]/connect/route.ts:19). Pages render err.message verbatim into <Alert>: app/sign-in/page.tsx:25, app/sign-up/page.tsx:34, app/forgot-password/page.tsx:26, app/dashboard/contacts/page.tsx:40, app/dashboard/device/page.tsx:53 — each with an additional hardcoded English literal fallback "Error". Result: the default-language (Vietnamese) senior-focused audience sees every failure — wrong password, bad Wi-Fi credentials, missing channel token — in English, exactly where clear guidance matters most. The dictionary in lib/i18n.tsx contains zero keys for these runtime errors.
proposal: Localize errors on the client, keyed by machine-readable data rather than server prose: (1) in lib/api.ts keep ApiError.status (and ideally an error code once the real BE lands); (2) add dict keys such as errInvalidCredentials, errInvalidEmail, errWifiFailed, errMissingFields, errGeneric (with a status placeholder) to lib/i18n.tsx; (3) in each catch, map ApiError.status/context to t(...) — e.g. sign-in 401 → t('errInvalidCredentials') — and replace the literal "Error" fallbacks with t('errGeneric'). For the contacts missing-fields case, build the message client-side from the known credentialFields so the field list can be joined per-locale.
verifierNote: All cites verified: lib/api.ts:40-43 throws ApiError with server `error` string or English `Request failed (${res.status})`; English-only mock errors at app/api/auth/sign-in/route.ts:8 ('Invalid credentials'), app/api/auth/sign-up/route.ts:7,11, app/api/device/wifi/route.ts:7 ('Failed to connect'), app/api/contacts/[id]/connect/route.ts:19 (interpolated missing-fields list). err.message rendered verbatim with hardcoded 'Error' fallback at app/sign-in/page.tsx:25, app/sign-up/page.tsx:34, app/forgot-password/page.tsx:25 (reviewer said :26 — off by one, immaterial), app/dashboard/contacts/page.tsx:40, app/dashboard/device/page.tsx:53. lib/i18n.tsx dict has zero runtime-error keys. The everyday path — sign-in wrong password → 401 'Invalid credentials' — is fully reachable (client only pre-validates on sign-up, app/sign-up/page.tsx:22-29). Requirements even pin English error strings in the contract (requirements.md 'Invalid credentials'), so the proposal's client-side status/context→t() mapping is the correct architecture. High is calibrated for the i18n dimension.

title: Logs tab has no time filter despite explicit requirement
description: requirements.md:34 states Logs must be "filterable by direction (in/out), status, time". The filter row at app/dashboard/logs/page.tsx:45-72 renders only two selects (direction, status). LogsQuery in lib/be.ts:79-83 has no time parameters, and /api/logs (app/api/logs/route.ts:13-24) only filters on direction and status. The i18n dictionary even defines an unused "time" key (lib/i18n.tsx:70/160). A developer inspecting an incident from yesterday must scroll the whole list; with the 50-entry cap they may not be able to reach older entries at all.
proposal: Add a third filter control — simplest: a preset range select (Last hour / Last 24h / Last 7 days / All, reusing the existing t("time") label) that maps to a `from` ISO timestamp; or from/to datetime-local inputs. Thread `from`/`to` through LogsAPI.list into the query string, and filter `l.timestamp >= from && l.timestamp <= to` in app/api/logs/route.ts.

title: Device page shows infinite spinner forever if the device fetch fails
description: load() at app/dashboard/device/page.tsx:35-37 is `DeviceAPI.info().then(setDevice).catch(() => {})` — the error is swallowed with no state change. Since line 59 renders `<Spinner />` whenever device is null, any failure of GET /api/device on first mount (network down, 500, expired token) leaves the user on a spinner permanently with no error message and no retry affordance. A failed manual Refresh (line 72) is equally silent: the button appears to do nothing and the user keeps looking at stale data with no indication.
proposal: Add an error state: on catch, set an error string; when device is null and error is set, render an Alert with the message and a Retry button calling load(). On refresh failure with existing data, keep the data but surface an inline error/toast (e.g. "Refresh failed — showing last known state"), and consider a lastUpdated timestamp next to the Refresh button.

title: Submit failure is completely silent — no catch, no error UI, unhandled promise rejection
description: submit() (app/dashboard/voice-training/page.tsx:103-114) wraps VoiceAPI.submitSample in try/finally with no catch. lib/api.ts:40-44 throws ApiError on any non-2xx response, and fetch rejects on network failure. When that happens the rejection propagates out of the async onClick handler as an unhandled promise rejection: the button flips back from 'Submitting…' to 'Submit' (finally sets busy=false) and the user gets zero feedback — no alert, no message. The recording is preserved (reset() is only reached on success) but the user has no way to know the upload failed; they will assume it was sent, and their sample never reaches the history list.
proposal: Add a catch that stores the error and render it in the existing <Alert> slot next to micError/success (e.g. a submitError state with an i18n string like 'Gửi thất bại, vui lòng thử lại' / 'Submit failed, please try again'). Keep the recorded blob so the user can retry with the same Submit button. Clear the error on retry/re-record/nextPrompt.

No error state exists for submit (only micError/success, page.tsx:18-20), so the rejection escapes the onClick as unhandled, finally flips busy=false (button reverts to 'Submit'), and reset()/loadSamples() are skipped — blob preserved but zero user feedback. The proposed submitError Alert matches the existing micError/success Alert pattern (page.tsx:133-142). title: Dashboard tab navigation has no aria-current; active tab is conveyed only visually
description: The tab nav (app/dashboard/layout.tsx:70-89) renders Links whose active state is expressed purely by classes — "border-lotus text-sen" vs "border-transparent text-slate-500" (lines 80-81). There is no aria-current="page", so a screen reader reads all four tabs identically and the user cannot tell which section they are in (compounded by the shared document title, see separate finding). The <nav> also has no accessible name. Fails WCAG 4.1.2 / fails to use the standard technique for 2.4.8.
proposal: Add aria-current={active ? "page" : undefined} to each Link (line 74-83) and aria-label={t("…")} (e.g. "Dashboard sections") on the <nav> at line 70. This is a two-attribute change; the existing pathname.startsWith(href) boolean (line 72) already computes the state.

title: Expandable log rows lack aria-expanded/aria-controls; expansion state is chevron-icon-only
description: Each log row toggle (app/dashboard/logs/page.tsx:84-105) is correctly a <button>, but it exposes no aria-expanded and no aria-controls linking to the payload panel (106-125). The only expansion cue is swapping ChevronDown/ChevronRight lucide icons (88-92), which have no text alternative. A screen reader user activating the row hears no state change and has no programmatic relationship to the revealed payload/response region. title: Network failures bypass ApiError normalization and surface raw browser errors to users
description: api() only normalizes HTTP error responses (lib/api.ts:40-44). The fetch call at lib/api.ts:33 is not wrapped, so a network-level failure (offline, DNS, server down, CORS) rejects with the browser's raw TypeError ('Failed to fetch' / 'Load failed' in Safari). Every page renders err.message verbatim: app/sign-in/page.tsx:25 `setError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : "Error")`, same pattern in app/dashboard/contacts/page.tsx:39, app/dashboard/device/page.tsx:52, app/sign-up/page.tsx, app/forgot-password/page.tsx. Users of this Vietnamese-default app see an untranslated, technical browser-internal string, and calling code cannot distinguish 'network unreachable' from an HTTP error because the thrown value is not an ApiError and has no .status.
proposal: Wrap the fetch in try/catch and re-throw a normalized error, e.g. `throw new ApiError(0, "network")` (or a dedicated NetworkError class). In the UI layer, map status 0 to an i18n key like errNetwork ('Không thể kết nối máy chủ'). This keeps the be.ts contract of 'everything thrown is ApiError' true.
verifierNote: lib/api.ts:33 `const res = await fetch(...)` is not wrapped; only `!res.ok` at lib/api.ts:40-44 produces ApiError, so a rejected fetch (offline/DNS/CORS) propagates the browser TypeError. UI renders it verbatim: app/sign-in/page.tsx:25 `setError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : "Error")`, same at app/dashboard/contacts/page.tsx:40 and app/dashboard/device/page.tsx:53. No .status on the thrown value, so callers cannot distinguish network from HTTP errors, and the string is untranslated (lib/i18n.tsx vi-default). Proposal (ApiError(0,...) + i18n mapping) fits the existing ApiError pattern. Medium is fair — reachable today by any offline user.

title: No 401 handling in transport: expired/invalid token mid-session leaves user on dashboard with silently empty data
description: Nothing in the transport layer reacts to a 401. api() throws ApiError(401,...) like any other error (lib/api.ts:40-44); the only token-invalidation path is the one-shot AuthAPI.me() on mount (lib/auth.tsx:35-38), which clears the token but only runs at page load. Mid-session, if the token becomes invalid (real-BE expiry, or user clearing/corrupting localStorage 'token'), every data fetch fails with 401 and pages swallow it into empty states: app/dashboard/contacts/page.tsx:19 `.catch(() => setChannels([]))`, app/dashboard/logs/page.tsx:32, app/dashboard/voice-training/page.tsx:30. The user stays 'signed in' on a dashboard showing empty lists with no explanation, violating the spirit of requirements.md §3 line 15 ('Protected dashboard routes — redirect to /sign-in if not authenticated'). With the mock this is latent (mock tokens never expire), but the whole point of lib/api.ts per README is to swap in a real BE unchanged.
proposal: In api(), when res.status === 401 and the path is not an /auth/* endpoint, clear the stored token (setToken(null)) and dispatch a sign-out (e.g. window.dispatchEvent(new Event('auth:unauthorized')) that AuthProvider listens to, calling setUser(null) so the existing dashboard-layout redirect at app/dashboard/layout.tsx:30-32 kicks in). Still throw the ApiError so callers can stop spinners.
verifierNote: Verified: nothing in lib/api.ts reacts to 401 (lib/api.ts:40-44 throws generically); the only token-clearing path is the mount-time AuthAPI.me() at lib/auth.tsx:35-38. Dashboard pages swallow fetch errors into empty states: app/dashboard/contacts/page.tsx:19 `.catch(() => setChannels([]))`, app/dashboard/logs/page.tsx:32, app/dashboard/voice-training/page.tsx:30,36, and device swallows entirely (app/dashboard/device/page.tsx:36 `.catch(() => {})` = infinite spinner). The layout redirect at app/dashboard/layout.tsx:30-32 only fires when `user` is null, which never happens mid-session. Latent with the mock (tokens never expire, lib/mock/token.ts), but lib/api.ts/be.ts are explicitly the swap-in-place real-BE layer (lib/be.ts:1-10, README.md:31-45), so medium for a design gap in that layer is defensible. Proposal matches existing architecture.

title: Mock store + setTimeout state model breaks on Vercel serverless despite 'Vercel-deployable' requirement
description: requirements.md §6 line 136-137 states the app must be Vercel-deployable with the mock as the default backend. The mock's state lives in globalThis (lib/mock/store.ts:4, 84-87) — correct for sharing across route-handler module instances in `next dev`, but on Vercel each serverless instance has its own globalThis: a POST /api/contacts/:id/connect handled by one lambda is invisible to a GET /api/contacts served by another, so connect/disconnect, Wi-Fi changes, and submitted samples randomly 'disappear' on refresh. Worse, app/api/voice-training/samples/route.ts:30-32 schedules `setTimeout(() => { sample.status = ... }, 8000)` after returning the response; on serverless the function is frozen once the response is sent, so the timeout typically never fires and samples stay 'pending' forever — and the voice-training page polls indefinitely while any sample is pending (app/dashboard/voice-training/page.tsx:42).
proposal: Make sample status derivation stateless instead of timer-based: store only createdAt, and in the GET handler (and the POST response) compute status from age, e.g. `age > 8000 ? (hash(id) % 10 ? "processed" : "failed") : "pending"` — deterministic, works per-instance, and survives serverless freezing. Additionally document in README that other mock mutations are per-instance on Vercel, or seed mutations idempotently.

Age-derived status proposal is sound and stateless. Medium confirmed.

title: No 401 handling mid-session — expired/invalid token leaves user in a silently broken dashboard
description: The token is validated exactly once, on AuthProvider mount (lib/auth.tsx:29-39). After that, nothing in the app reacts to a 401: lib/api.ts:40-44 throws ApiError(401) like any other error, and every dashboard consumer swallows it — contacts sets an empty list (app/dashboard/contacts/page.tsx:19 `.catch(() => setChannels([]))`), device ignores it entirely (app/dashboard/device/page.tsx:36 `.catch(() => {})`), logs sets [] (app/dashboard/logs/page.tsx:32). The mock masks this because base64 tokens never expire, but requirements.md:137 explicitly plans an env-based swap to a real backend, where token expiry/revocation mid-session is routine. The user would then sit on a dashboard where every tab shows empty data or silent failures, with no redirect to /sign-in — violating requirements.md:15 ('Protected dashboard routes — redirect to /sign-in if not authenticated').
proposal: Centralize 401 handling in the transport: in api() (lib/api.ts), when res.status === 401 and the path is not an auth endpoint, clear the token (setToken(null)) and notify the AuthProvider (e.g., a registered onUnauthorized callback that sets user=null, which makes app/dashboard/layout.tsx:30-32 redirect to /sign-in). Alternatively catch ApiError with status 401 in AuthProvider via a shared event emitter. Keep the throw so callers can still show messages.

But 'high' is miscalibrated: the mock token is stateless base64 with no expiry or revocation (lib/mock/token.ts:4-19, app/api/auth/me/route.ts:5-8), so a mid-session 401 cannot occur in the shipped app today — it is a latent defect that only manifests after the real-BE swap. Downgrade to medium; the centralized-401 proposal itself is sound.

title: Transient me() failure on app load silently deletes the session token
description: lib/auth.tsx:35-38 runs AuthAPI.me() on mount and `.catch(() => setToken(null))` on ANY rejection. fetch rejects with a TypeError on network failure (offline, DNS blip, backend restart) and api() also throws for 500/503 — none of which mean the token is invalid. A user who reloads the app during a brief connectivity hiccup has their token permanently deleted from localStorage and is forced to sign in again, even though their session was valid. With the real backend (requirements.md:137) this makes sessions fragile on flaky mobile connections.
proposal: Only clear the token when the failure is an actual auth rejection: `.catch((err) => { if (err instanceof ApiError && err.status === 401) setToken(null); })` (ApiError is already exported from lib/api.ts:13). For network/server errors, keep the token and surface a retry state (or simply leave user=null without destroying the token so the next reload can succeed).

ApiError is exported (lib/api.ts:13) so the proposed status===401 guard is a one-line, pattern-consistent fix. Medium is fair for a logic bug that conflates transport failure with auth rejection.

title: Auth error messages bypass i18n — Vietnamese-default users see raw English server strings, fallback is hardcoded "Error"
description: All three auth pages render `err instanceof Error ? err.message : "Error"` (app/sign-in/page.tsx:25, app/sign-up/page.tsx:34, app/forgot-password/page.tsx:25). err.message is the mock backend's English string — 'Invalid credentials' (app/api/auth/sign-in/route.ts:8), 'Invalid email' / 'Password must be at least 6 characters' (app/api/auth/sign-up/route.ts:7,11) — or the transport's English 'Request failed (500)' (lib/api.ts:42). Only fall back to the raw server message when no mapping exists (real BE may send localized messages later).

title: Secret credential fields (access tokens) rendered as plain text inputs
description: The credential form renders every field via `<Input key={f} label={f} ... />` (app/dashboard/contacts/page.tsx:94-101) with no `type` or `autoComplete` prop, and the Input component defaults to a bare `<input>` (components/ui.tsx:56-64), i.e. type="text". The fields are secrets — `accessToken`, `pageAccessToken`, `botToken` (lib/mock/store.ts:21,27,33) — so tokens are displayed in cleartext (shoulder-surfable, visible in screen shares) and eligible for browser autofill/history since autocomplete is not disabled.

Extend the Input component to pass these through — it already spreads ...props so only the call site needs changing.

But severity is miscalibrated: the tokens are user-typed, never persisted client-side, and the exposure is shoulder-surfing/autofill only — no transport or storage vulnerability. title: Required 'error' channel status is unreachable dead code in the mock, and the error message string is never shown
description: Requirements mandate a 'connected / not connected / error' status indicator (requirements.md:24). The UI supports it — page.tsx:65-66 renders a red 'Lỗi' badge when `ch.error` is truthy, and Channel has `error?: string | null` (lib/types.ts:14) — but nothing ever sets it: the seed data gives no channel an error (lib/mock/store.ts:16-35), the connect route only clears it (`channel.error = null`, app/api/contacts/[id]/connect/route.ts:24), and disconnect never touches it (disconnect/route.ts:13). So the error state can never appear during FE development, meaning the third of three required states is unverified. Additionally, even when `error` is a string, the UI discards its content — only the generic badge text is shown, and the badge branch hides whether the channel is still connected (page.tsx:65-71).

In the UI, show the error detail (e.g. small red text under the badge or a title tooltip) and keep the connected/disconnected badge visible alongside the error badge so the correct action button state is explainable.

UI supports it (page.tsx:65-66 red badge on ch.error; lib/types.ts:14 error?: string|null) but nothing sets it: seed has no error on any channel (lib/mock/store.ts:16-35), connect only clears it (`channel.error = null`, app/api/contacts/[id]/connect/route.ts:24), disconnect never touches error (disconnect/route.ts:13-14). The badge shows only t("channelError") ('Lỗi', i18n.tsx:40) and the error branch suppresses the connected/disconnected badge (page.tsx:65-71) while the button still keys off ch.connected (page.tsx:73). title: Credential form labels are raw API field names (oaId, pageAccessToken) — not human-readable or localized
description: The connect modal renders `label={f}` straight from `credentialFields` (app/dashboard/contacts/page.tsx:94-101), so users see machine identifiers 'oaId', 'accessToken', 'pageId', 'pageAccessToken', 'botToken' (lib/mock/store.ts:21,27,33) as form labels, with no placeholder or help text about where to obtain these values. title: Clicking the modal overlay discards typed credentials without warning, even mid-submit
description: The connect Modal closes on any overlay click (components/ui.tsx:149-151 `onClick={onClose}`) and the page's onClose is `setEditing(null)` (app/dashboard/contacts/page.tsx:88), which unmounts the form; reopening resets creds to {} (page.tsx:25). A user who has pasted/typed two long tokens and mis-clicks outside loses everything silently. The Cancel button and overlay also stay active while `busy` is true, so the modal can be dismissed mid-request — a subsequent failure calls setError on a modal that is no longer visible, and the user never sees whether the connect succeeded or failed until the badge maybe changes.

(Minimal version: pass a no-op onClose while busy and disable the Cancel button with `disabled={busy}`.)

Neither the Cancel button (page.tsx:104-110, no disabled prop) nor the overlay is gated on busy, so dismissal mid-request is possible; connect's catch then calls setError (page.tsx:40) but the Modal renders null once editing is null, and openConnect clears error on reopen (page.tsx:26), so the failure alert is never seen. title: No error boundaries or not-found page anywhere in the App Router tree
description: The repo contains no app/error.tsx, no app/global-error.tsx, no app/not-found.tsx, and no dashboard-level error boundary (verified by full file listing: only layout.tsx/page.tsx files exist under app/). Multiple reviewers flagged unhandled promise rejections (voice submit, contacts disconnect), but nobody flagged that any *render-time* throw — e.g. useAuth() used outside its provider (lib/auth.tsx:70 throws), a malformed API payload hitting `new Date(s.createdAt)`/`JSON.stringify(log.payload)`, or any future bug — bubbles to Next.js's default unstyled error screen (a blank white page in production) with no recovery affordance, in neither Vietnamese nor English. For a product aimed at seniors this is the worst possible failure mode, and it is one file away from being fixed. A typo'd URL (e.g. /dashbord) similarly renders the framework's default 404 instead of a branded, localized page.

Optionally add a dashboard/error.tsx so tab crashes keep the header/nav intact.

But every concrete crash trigger cited is implausible: useAuth's throw (lib/auth.tsx:70) is unreachable because Providers wraps the entire tree in the root layout (app/layout.tsx:19, app/providers.tsx:8-10); `new Date(s.createdAt)` (voice-training/page.tsx:201) never throws — it yields Invalid Date; `JSON.stringify(log.payload)` (logs/page.tsx:113) can only throw on circular/BigInt values, impossible for JSON-parsed API data. title: Lint script is broken (ESLint not installed) and there is no CI

title: No data-fetching layer: five hand-rolled useEffect fetchers with divergent error policies and zero caching
description: Every tab reimplements fetch-on-mount with a different failure policy: contacts swallows errors into [] (app/dashboard/contacts/page.tsx:19), device ignores errors entirely leaving an infinite spinner (app/dashboard/device/page.tsx:36), logs and voice coerce errors to [] (app/dashboard/logs/page.tsx:32, voice-training/page.tsx:30,36). None dedupe, cache, cancel, or revalidate — switching tabs refetches everything from scratch and back-to-back filter changes race (already flagged individually). No reviewer owned the root cause: the absence of any shared async-state abstraction (SWR/React Query, or even a small useQuery hook returning {data, error, loading, refetch}). Fixing the ~10 flagged per-page symptoms one by one will re-duplicate the same logic six times.
proposal: Introduce one shared hook (SWR is the lightest fit for Next.js) or a hand-rolled useQuery in lib/ that wraps lib/be.ts calls with loading/error/data states, AbortController cancellation, focus revalidation and interval polling options. Migrate all five pages to it; the flagged race conditions, swallowed errors, and missing retry/refresh affordances then get fixed in exactly one place.

None use AbortController or caching (verified across all pages and lib/api.ts:21-46), and logs/page.tsx:27-33 refetches on every filter change with no cancellation, so back-to-back changes can race. Five hand-rolled fetchers with three distinct failure policies is an accurate root-cause framing, and a single shared hook wrapping lib/be.ts is proportionate for this codebase. Medium confirmed.

title: Fully client-rendered app with a serial auth→redirect→data waterfall of spinners
description: Every route is "use client" and route protection is a client-side useEffect (app/dashboard/layout.tsx:30-34 renders a bare Spinner until me() resolves). A cold load of the app serializes: HTML/JS download → hydrate → read localStorage token → GET /api/auth/me (lib/auth.tsx:35) → client redirect / → /dashboard → server redirect to /dashboard/contacts (app/dashboard/page.tsx:4) → GET /api/contacts — four sequential round trips, each showing a different spinner. Because the token lives only in localStorage, no middleware or server component can ever short-circuit this; the App Router is used purely as a client-side SPA shell. Individual findings covered localStorage security and deep-link loss, but nobody flagged the structural rendering/perf consequence users feel on every visit.
proposal: Store the session token in a cookie (httpOnly once the real BE lands) so a middleware.ts can redirect unauthenticated /dashboard/* requests server-side before any JS loads, collapsing the spinner chain. Meanwhile, kick off the tab's data fetch in parallel with me() instead of gating all children on auth resolution, and add route loading.tsx skeletons instead of bare spinners.
verifierNote: Waterfall verified: dashboard layout gates all children on auth (app/dashboard/layout.tsx:34 `if (loading || !user) return <Spinner />`), auth resolves via client-side me() after reading localStorage (lib/auth.tsx:29-39, token from lib/api.ts:3-6 localStorage), home page client-redirects after auth resolves (app/page.tsx:12-15), /dashboard server-redirects to /dashboard/contacts (app/dashboard/page.tsx:4), then contacts fetches (contacts/page.tsx:18-22). No middleware.ts exists; a localStorage-only token indeed prevents any server-side short-circuit. Minor overstatement — app/dashboard/page.tsx and app/layout.tsx are server components — but every interactive route is 'use client' and the structural consequence is real. Cookie+middleware proposal is the standard fix and forward-compatible with the real BE. Medium is right.

title: No getUserMedia/MediaRecorder feature detection; every failure mode collapses into a misleading 'grant mic permission' message
description: startRecording (lines 57-83) calls navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia and `new MediaRecorder(stream)` with no capability check. On an insecure origin — e.g. the hub served over plain http on the LAN next to the ESP32, a very plausible deployment — navigator.mediaDevices is undefined; on browsers without MediaRecorder it is a ReferenceError. Both, plus NotFoundError (no microphone), NotAllowedError (denied), and NotReadableError (mic busy), land in the same bare `catch` (line 80) that shows only t("micDenied") = 'Please grant mic permission in your browser' (lib/i18n.tsx:55) — wrong guidance for four of the five causes, and the core feature of Tab 2 silently cannot work with no path forward. Related: mimeType is left to browser default, so Safari produces audio/mp4 while the upload filename says .webm (the filename half was flagged; the undetected unsupported-API half was not).
proposal: Before rendering the Record button, check `typeof MediaRecorder !== 'undefined' && navigator.mediaDevices?.getUserMedia` and show a localized 'recording not supported in this browser / requires HTTPS' notice if absent. In the catch, branch on DOMException.name (NotAllowedError vs NotFoundError vs NotReadableError) to show distinct localized messages, and pick a supported mimeType via MediaRecorder.isTypeSupported, propagating it to the upload filename/content type.
verifierNote: Verified: startRecording (voice-training/page.tsx:57-83) calls navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia (line 61) and new MediaRecorder (line 62) with no feature detection; on insecure origins mediaDevices is undefined (TypeError) and a missing MediaRecorder global is a ReferenceError — both land in the bare catch at line 80 along with NotAllowedError/NotFoundError/NotReadableError, all rendering only t("micDenied") (line 135; lib/i18n.tsx:55,146). Tiny nit: the string actually opens with 'Microphone unavailable.' before the grant-permission instruction, so NotFoundError is half-covered — but the guidance is flatly wrong for HTTPS-required and unsupported-browser cases, which are plausible for a LAN-deployed hub. The mimeType half also checks out: recorder created with no mimeType, blob typed recorder.mimeType || 'audio/webm' (line 67), upload filename hardcoded 'sample.webm' (lib/be.ts:68). Medium confirmed.

title: Button has no loading prop; busy-label pattern hand-rolled in 6 places and disabled styling is inconsistent
description: Every submitting form re-implements `{busy ? t("loading") : label}`: app/sign-in/page.tsx:58-60, app/sign-up/page.tsx:67-69, app/forgot-password/page.tsx:54-56, app/dashboard/contacts/page.tsx:111-113, app/dashboard/device/page.tsx:191-193, and voice submit (voice-training/page.tsx:177-179, which swaps the label but keeps the Send icon). Meanwhile disabled treatment differs per variant (ui.tsx:17-21): primary uses `disabled:opacity-50`, danger swaps to `bg-red-300`, secondary/ghost only dim text — and hover classes are not gated, so a disabled primary button still darkens on hover (`hover:bg-sen-dark` matches disabled elements), signaling interactivity it doesn't have. Result: subtly different 'busy' appearances per page and misleading hover feedback.
proposal: Add `loading?: boolean` to Button that disables the button and renders a small inline spinner beside the label (keeps width stable, removes the icon-swap inconsistency); gate hovers with `enabled:hover:*` (Tailwind 4 supports `enabled:`); unify disabled treatment (e.g. opacity-50 across variants). Replace all six hand-rolled busy ternaries.

Disabled treatment diverges per variant exactly as cited (ui.tsx:17-21): opacity-50 / bg-red-300 / text-slate-400. Hover classes are unconditioned (`hover:bg-sen-dark` at ui.tsx:17) and CSS :hover matches disabled elements, so a disabled primary button does darken on hover. `enabled:` variant exists in Tailwind (v3.1+), proposal is sound.

title: Modal primitive lacks Escape close, scroll lock, close affordance — and backdrop click silently discards typed form data
description: Modal (components/ui.tsx:135-161) is a bare fixed div: no Escape-key handling, no body scroll lock, no visible close (X) button, no portal, and the entire backdrop closes on any click (ui.tsx:149-151). In the contacts credential modal (app/dashboard/contacts/page.tsx:86-116) and the Wi-Fi modal (app/dashboard/device/page.tsx:162-196), one stray click outside while typing a token/password closes the dialog and wipes the input (openConnect resets creds at contacts/page.tsx:24-28). The logs page hand-rolls select styling (app/dashboard/logs/page.tsx:37-38) that diverges from Input (py-1.5 vs py-2, no focus ring vs ring — components/ui.tsx:59), so paired form controls look and behave differently. Empty states are ad-hoc bare paragraphs: voice history `

title: Base 17px 'senior-friendly' font is defeated — nearly all content is text-sm/text-xs
description: globals.css:17-20 raises the root font to 17px explicitly for 'senior-friendly readability', but the system then sets almost everything below base: Button text-sm (components/ui.tsx:26), Input text and labels text-sm (ui.tsx:51,59), tab labels text-sm (app/dashboard/layout.tsx:78), page descriptions text-sm (contacts/page.tsx:58, device/page.tsx:70), all device data text-sm (device/page.tsx:88), and metadata text-xs (~12.8px effective; voice-training/page.tsx:200, logs/page.tsx:102). title: Input uses label text as DOM id fallback, producing invalid and collision-prone ids
description: components/ui.tsx:45 does `const inputId = id || label;` — no page passes `id`, so the rendered i18n label becomes the element id. Vietnamese labels contain spaces/diacritics/parens: id="Mật khẩu" (lib/i18n.tsx:16), id="Tên mạng (SSID)" (lib/i18n.tsx:84) — whitespace in id values is invalid HTML, breaks CSS/querySelector targeting, and any two inputs sharing a label string on one page/modal would produce duplicate ids with mis-associated labels (the pattern makes this a landmine for every new form). Also, when `label` is set the id changes whenever the user toggles language, churning the DOM identity of a focused field.
proposal: Use React's useId(): `const reactId = React.useId(); const inputId = id ?? reactId;` — guaranteed unique, language-independent, valid. One-line fix in the primitive covers every form in the app.
verifierNote: ui.tsx:45 is exactly `const inputId = id || label;` and no caller passes id (verified all Inputs in sign-in/up/forgot/contacts/device). Labels contain spaces: 'Mật khẩu' (lib/i18n.tsx:16) and 'Tên mạng (SSID)' (i18n wifiName) become id values; ASCII whitespace in id is invalid HTML5. useId proposal is correct and one line. One overstatement: language toggle changes the id *attribute* but React does not remount the element (no key change), so focus is not lost and htmlFor/id stay paired — 'churning DOM identity' is wrong in effect, but the core invalid-id/collision-landmine claim holds.

title: Weak/mixed active-tab indication and hidden account identity on mobile header
description: Active tab styling (app/dashboard/layout.tsx:79-81) mixes brand hues — pink underline (`border-lotus`) with blue text (`text-sen`) — while inactive-hover also turns text blue (`hover:text-sen`), so on hover the only difference between an inactive and the active tab is a 2px underline; there is no aria-current, background, or weight change. On mobile the bar relies on `overflow-x-auto` (layout.tsx:70) with no scroll affordance (no fade/snap), and for a developer (4 tabs with icons) the last tab can sit off-screen with no visual hint. Separately, the header hides the signed-in email and role badge below sm (layout.tsx:55 `hidden ... sm:flex`), so mobile users — the primary form factor for a home-device companion app — cannot see which account they're using or why the Logs tab does/doesn't appear; sign-out is an icon-only button whose label lives in a desktop-only `title` tooltip (layout.tsx:61-67).

On mobile, add edge-fade masks on the scrollable nav or switch to an equal-width grid for ≤4 tabs. Surface the account (email or avatar-with-menu containing email/role/sign-out) at all breakpoints.

Nav is bare `overflow-x-auto` (layout.tsx:70) with no fade/snap; 4 icon+Vietnamese-label tabs ('Huấn luyện giọng nói') plausibly overflow 375px. Email+role badge wrapper is `hidden ... sm:flex` (layout.tsx:55), and sign-out is icon-only with only a title attr (61-67). All accurate; medium fits.

title: html lang attribute is hardcoded to "vi" and never syncs with the selected language
description: app/layout.tsx:17 renders <html lang="vi"> statically, and setLang in lib/i18n.tsx:215-218 only updates React state and localStorage — it never touches document.documentElement.lang. After a user switches to English, the entire English UI is declared as Vietnamese: screen readers pick the wrong pronunciation voice (notably bad for a product aimed at seniors), browser translation prompts misfire, and spellcheck/hyphenation use the wrong rules. The lens-relevant contract (vi default + user-switchable en, requirements.md:8) implies the document language should follow the switch.
proposal: In I18nProvider, add an effect that mirrors state to the DOM: `useEffect(() => { document.documentElement.lang = lang; }, [lang])` in lib/i18n.tsx. If the cookie-based persistence proposal is adopted, also set the initial lang attribute server-side in app/layout.tsx from the cookie so first paint is correct too.

Proposal (effect mirroring lang to DOM) is minimal and correct. Medium stands.

title: Language preference read post-hydration causes a Vietnamese flash for English users on every load
description: I18nProvider initializes lang to "vi" (lib/i18n.tsx:208) and only reads the stored preference inside a client useEffect (lib/i18n.tsx:210-213). This correctly avoids an SSR hydration mismatch, but it means a user who chose English sees the whole UI render in Vietnamese first and then flip to English after hydration — on every page load and full refresh. requirements.md:138 explicitly allows 'cookie/localStorage' persistence; only localStorage was chosen, which makes the preference invisible to the server.
proposal: Persist the language in a cookie (in addition to or instead of localStorage): setLang writes `document.cookie = "lang=..."`; the root layout (app/layout.tsx, a server component) reads it via next/headers cookies() and passes it as initialLang to Providers/I18nProvider, also setting <html lang={initialLang}>. First paint then matches the saved language with no flash and no hydration mismatch. A lighter alternative is a beforeInteractive inline script, but the cookie route also fixes SSR'd html lang.

Cookie + server-read initialLang proposal is sound and also enables finding 1's SSR fix. Medium is fair: visible on every load for the English audience.

title: Raw API credential field names (oaId, pageAccessToken, botToken) used as form labels in both languages

The proposed keyed-map-with-raw-fallback pattern is exactly what app/dashboard/device/page.tsx:17-23,149 already does for component names, so it fits the codebase. Medium confirmed.

title: Submitted voice sample does not record which language variant of the prompt was read
description: The prompt shown to the user is language-dependent — `lang === "vi" ? prompt.text_vi : prompt.text_en` (app/dashboard/voice-training/page.tsx:146) — but the submission sends only promptId + audio (lib/be.ts:68-76, submit at page.tsx:107). Since every prompt has two textual variants (lib/mock/store.ts:89-115), promptId alone is ambiguous: the backend cannot know whether the recording is of the Vietnamese or English sentence, which matters for a voice-training corpus. requirements.md:30 says 'audio + the matched example text sent to backend' — the matched text (or at minimum its language) is never transmitted. Note the correctly-wired part: prompt display and history rendering (page.tsx:146,198) do react to language switches, so display itself is fine.

Every prompt has both variants (lib/mock/store.ts:89-115), so promptId is ambiguous about which sentence was read. requirements.md:30: 'audio + the matched example text sent to backend' — the matched text is indeed never transmitted. Capturing lang at record time (not submit time) is the right detail. Medium confirmed.

title: Logs fetch errors are rendered as the 'no matching logs' empty state
description: The fetch effect uses `.catch(() => setLogs([]))` (app/dashboard/logs/page.tsx:32), so a network failure or 5xx renders the same UI as a genuinely empty result: `t("noLogs")` — "Không có nhật ký phù hợp" (line 77). For a developer-facing debugging tool this is actively misleading: an outage of the logs endpoint looks like "your filters matched nothing", sending the developer chasing filter values instead of the real failure.

title: Stale-response race when changing log filters quickly
description: The effect at app/dashboard/logs/page.tsx:27-33 fires a new LogsAPI.list on every direction/status change but has no cancellation or staleness guard. If a user flips direction from "in" to "out" while the first request is in flight, and the first response arrives last (realistic with a real BE where a broader query is slower), setLogs applies the stale "in" result while the UI selects show "out" — the list silently contradicts the active filters. The full reset to null on every change (line 29) also blows away the list for a spinner flash on each filter tweak.
proposal: Add an ignore flag in the effect (`let cancelled = false; ... .then(d => { if (!cancelled) setLogs(d); }); return () => { cancelled = true; }`) or an AbortController passed through to fetch. Optionally keep previous data visible with a subtle loading indicator instead of `setLogs(null)`.

Practically unlikely against the same-origin mock, but lib/be.ts:1-10 documents the app is built to swap to a real BE, where out-of-order responses are realistic. Standard fix proposed is correct. Medium is acceptable.

title: Wi-Fi modal retains typed password, SSID, and stale error across close/reopen
description: Closing the Wi-Fi modal via Cancel (app/dashboard/device/page.tsx:184-190), backdrop click, or the Modal onClose (line 164) only calls setWifiOpen(false); ssid/password are cleared solely on success (lines 49-50) and error solely at the start of the next submit (line 44). So after a failed attempt the user reopens the modal to find the old red error alert still displayed and the previously typed Wi-Fi password still sitting (masked) in the field. Besides the confusing stale error, the plaintext password lingers in component state and the DOM for the rest of the session.

title: Mock voice-sample status transition uses setTimeout in a route handler — breaks on Vercel (§6)
description: requirements.md:137 requires the app to be Vercel-deployable with the mock serving until the real BE lands. The mock POST /api/voice-training/samples handler schedules sample.status = processed/failed via setTimeout 8s AFTER returning the response (app/api/voice-training/samples/route.ts:30-32). On Vercel serverless, execution is frozen/terminated once the response is sent, so the timer never fires reliably (and the in-memory store isn't shared across lambda instances anyway). Consequence in a deployed demo: every submitted sample stays "pending" forever, and the voice-training page's pending-poll effect (app/dashboard/voice-training/page.tsx:41-45) keeps refetching every 5 seconds indefinitely — the §4 requirement "history list ... with status (pending/processed/failed)" is only observable on a local dev server.

"processed" : "failed". This keeps identical local behavior, works per-request on Vercel, and stays deterministic for a given sample. Note the same single-instance caveat for channel connect state in README's mock notes.

title: reset() after await in submit clobbers a newer recording — mic can stay live behind an 'idle' UI
description: While busy=true, only the Submit button is disabled (page.tsx:177); Re-record (line 174) and, after it, Record remain clickable. Sequence on a slow network: click Submit → click Re-record (back to idle) → click Record (recState='recording', new MediaRecorder live) → the original submit promise resolves and unconditionally runs setSuccess(true); reset(); (lines 108-109). reset() (lines 87-94) forces recState='idle' and nulls blobRef without stopping any recorder, so the UI now shows the idle Record button while the previous MediaRecorder and its mic stream are still running (browser recording indicator stays on). Clicking Record again overwrites recorderRef (line 77), orphaning the live recorder/stream until page unmount; its eventual onstop also fires setRecState('recorded') at an arbitrary time, corrupting the state machine.
proposal: Make submit's success path state-aware: only call reset() if recState is still 'recorded' (e.g. guard with a ref token per recording, or simply disable Re-record while busy). Additionally have reset()/startRecording stop any existing recorderRef.current whose state is 'recording' before replacing it, so no code path can orphan a live mic stream.
verifierNote: Verified: only Submit has disabled={busy} (page.tsx:177); Re-record (line 174) and Record (line 152) stay clickable while the submit promise is in flight. submit's success path unconditionally runs setSuccess(true); reset() (lines 108-109), and reset() (87-94) forces recState='idle' and nulls blobRef without touching recorderRef — so a newer recording made during the await is clobbered, and a still-live MediaRecorder sits behind an idle UI. Clicking Record then overwrites recorderRef (line 77) and the unmount cleanup (line 49) only stops recorderRef.current, so the orphaned stream leaks. One sub-detail is off: the orphaned recorder's onstop never fires (nothing ever calls stop() on it or ends its tracks), so the 'onstop fires at an arbitrary time' corruption path doesn't occur — but the headline clobber/live-mic/orphan bugs are real. Medium stands.

title: Transient samples-fetch failure wipes the whole history to 'No samples yet' and permanently kills polling
description: loadSamples (page.tsx:27-31) does .catch(() => setSamples([])). The polling effect (lines 41-45) runs setInterval(loadSamples, 5000) only while samples?.some(s => s.status === 'pending'). If one poll fails (network blip, sleeping laptop, expired token), samples becomes [], the UI silently replaces the entire history list with the empty-state 'No samples yet.' (lines 188-189), and — because [] contains no pending item — the effect tears down the interval and never restarts it. The user's real, still-pending sample vanishes from view and its status never updates again until they navigate away and back. The same catch also makes an initial load failure indistinguishable from a genuinely empty history.
proposal: On fetch failure, keep the previous samples state (catch → no-op or set a separate samplesError flag rendered as an inline error with a Retry button) instead of setSamples([]). Keep the poll alive across failures (track 'shouldPoll' from the last successful payload, optionally with capped backoff after consecutive failures) so a single blip doesn't freeze pending statuses forever.

One transient failure therefore replaces real history with the empty state and freezes pending statuses until navigation or a new submit. Facts and proposal check out; medium is right.

title: Unmount cleanup captures stale audioUrl (always null) — object URL leaks; mic stream also leaks if MediaRecorder setup throws
description: Two release-path bugs. (1) The unmount effect (page.tsx:47-53) has [] deps with an eslint-disable, so its cleanup closure captures audioUrl from the first render — always null. The 'if (audioUrl) URL.revokeObjectURL(audioUrl)' on line 50 is dead code: record a sample, switch tabs without pressing Re-record/Submit, and the blob URL (holding the entire audio blob in memory) is never revoked for the life of the page. (2) In startRecording (lines 60-83), the stream is acquired on line 61 before 'new MediaRecorder(stream)' on line 62; if the constructor throws (MediaRecorder unsupported — older Safari/iOS WebViews — or recorder.start() fails), the catch on line 80 only sets micError, never stopping the already-live stream's tracks: the browser's recording indicator stays on indefinitely while the UI tells the user to 'grant mic permission' (lib/i18n.tsx:55/146) — wrong guidance since permission was granted.
proposal: (1) Track the current URL in a ref (or store it alongside blobRef) and revoke via the ref in the unmount cleanup, removing the eslint-disable. (2) In startRecording, hold the stream in a local variable and add stream.getTracks().forEach(t => t.stop()) in the catch; also feature-detect (typeof MediaRecorder === 'undefined') before calling getUserMedia and show a distinct 'browser not supported' message instead of the permission message.

(2) startRecording acquires the stream (line 61) before 'new MediaRecorder(stream)' (line 62); if the constructor or start() (line 78) throws, the catch (80-82) only sets micError — recorderRef was never assigned, so even the unmount cleanup (line 49) can't stop the live stream, and micDenied text (lib/i18n.tsx:55/146) wrongly tells the user to grant permission. title: Prompts fetch failure renders a broken card: empty quoted sentence, recordable, and Submit is a silent no-op

title: No elapsed-time indicator, no duration limits — a 0-length or hour-long take can be recorded and submitted
description: While recording, the only feedback is a Stop button and a pulsing red dot with 'Recording…' (page.tsx:160-170) — no elapsed timer. There is no minimum-duration or blob-size check anywhere: tapping Record then Stop immediately produces a near-empty blob that onstop happily accepts (lines 65-76) and submit() uploads without validating blob size or duration (lines 103-114); the mock (app/api/voice-training/samples/route.ts:16) accepts any Blob, so a useless empty sample enters history as 'pending'. title: Failed samples are a dead end — no retry affordance and no failure reason
description: A history row with status 'failed' renders only a red 'Thất bại/Failed' badge (page.tsx:118-125, rows at 192-206). The mock produces failed samples ~10% of the time (app/api/voice-training/samples/route.ts:31), so users will hit this state; today their only option is to notice the red badge, scroll up, and manually cycle nextPrompt (sequentially, lines 96-98) until they find the matching sentence.

'processed' : 'failed'); prompt advance is strictly sequential (page.tsx:96-98) so reaching a specific failed prompt requires manual cycling. title: Input primitive derives element id from label text (invalid/duplicate-prone) and never links its error message
description:
Input (components/ui.tsx:35-68) computes `const inputId = id || label` (line 45), so with Vietnamese labels the rendered id becomes e.g. id="Mật khẩu" or id="Tên mạng (SSID)" — ids containing whitespace are invalid HTML (WCAG 4.1.1 parsing), break CSS/getElementById-based tooling and testing, and any two Inputs sharing a label text on one page silently produce duplicate ids that corrupt label association. No call site passes an explicit id (checked: all usages in sign-in, sign-up, forgot-password, contacts modal, device Wi-Fi modal rely on the label fallback). Separately, the error message

(line 65) is rendered with no id, no aria-describedby on the input, and no aria-invalid — so the component's own error mechanism is invisible to screen readers (WCAG 3.3.1).
proposal:
Use React 19's useId(): `const autoId = React.useId(); const inputId = id ?? autoId;`. For errors: give the

id={`${inputId}-error`}, and set aria-invalid={!!error || undefined} and aria-describedby={error ? `${inputId}-error` : undefined} on the input.
verifierNote: Facts verified: components/ui.tsx:45 `const inputId = id || label` yields whitespace/diacritic ids like id="Mật khẩu" (i18n.tsx:16) and id="Tên mạng (SSID)" (i18n.tsx:84); grep confirms no call site passes id=. But practical impact is overstated: browsers match label htmlFor against the id string literally, so label association WORKS today despite the invalid id; no page currently renders two Inputs with the same label (sign-up's three labels differ, modal credentialFields are distinct); WCAG 4.1.1 is obsolete in 2.2. And the error-message half concerns dead code — grep shows `error=` is passed by zero call sites, so ui.tsx:65 is never rendered. useId + aria-describedby is correct hardening of the primitive but fixes no user-observable defect now. severityOverride: low.

title: All routes share one static Vietnamese document title and the dashboard has no h1, degrading route announcements
description: Metadata is defined only in the root layout (app/layout.tsx:5-9); no page or nested layout exports its own title, so every route — sign-in, sign-up, and all four dashboard tabs — has the identical document.title. Next.js App Router's built-in route announcer announces document.title (falling back to h1) after client navigation, so switching tabs announces the same string every time, giving screen reader users no confirmation of where they landed. The dashboard also has no h1 at all: the header renders the app name as a <span> (app/dashboard/layout.tsx:45) and each tab page starts at <h2> (e.g. contacts/page.tsx:55), so heading navigation starts at level 2 with no level-1 root. There is also no skip link to bypass the repeated header/nav (WCAG 2.4.1, 2.4.2).
proposal: Since dashboard pages are client components, set the title per tab (e.g. a small useEffect/useDocumentTitle hook: `document.title = t(tabKey) + " — SEN"`, re-run on lang change), or add generateMetadata in per-tab layout files. Promote each tab page's h2 to h1 (or add an sr-only h1 in the dashboard layout). Add a skip-to-content link as the first focusable element in the dashboard layout targeting the <main> at line 91.

No skip link anywhere. Next.js route-announcer behavior described is accurate. Low severity and the proposal (per-tab document.title, h1 promotion, skip link) fit the client-component architecture.

title: Loading spinner is a bare div — loading states are invisible to screen readers
description: Spinner (components/ui.tsx:163-169) renders an empty animated div with no role, no accessible name, and no live semantics. It is used for every data-loading and auth-gating state (app/page.tsx:17, dashboard/layout.tsx:34, contacts:51, voice-training:116,187, logs:35,75, device:59). A screen reader user navigating during load perceives an empty page with no explanation.
proposal:
Add role="status" and an sr-only label to the wrapper: `
{loading text}
`. The dict already has a "loading" key (lib/i18n.tsx:93,181); since Spinner takes no props today, either accept an optional label prop or hardcode via useI18n.

title: Only /api/logs and /api/auth/me verify the token — all other mock endpoints are unauthenticated
description: app/api/logs/route.ts:5-12 checks the Bearer token and developer role, and app/api/auth/me/route.ts:5-8 checks the token, but no other handler does: GET /api/contacts (app/api/contacts/route.ts:4-6), POST connect/disconnect (app/api/contacts/[id]/connect/route.ts:4, disconnect/route.ts:4), GET /api/device (app/api/device/route.ts:4-6), POST /api/device/wifi (app/api/device/wifi/route.ts:4), and both voice-training routes (app/api/voice-training/prompts/route.ts:4, samples/route.ts:5 and :12) accept anonymous requests and even mutate shared store state. Beyond the (mock-acceptable) security gap, the inconsistency means the FE's 401 error paths for these five service groups are never exercised during development, so the 'swap to real BE' plan (README 'BE communication') ships untested unauthorized-handling — which matters because, per the finding above, pages currently render 401s as empty states.

But 'medium/security' is miscalibrated: this is a mock with no real data (acknowledged in lib/mock/token.ts:1, README.md:61), and the written contract itself only specifies an Authorization header for GET /api/auth/me (requirements.md:57-58) and 'developer only' for logs (requirements.md:99) — the other endpoints document no 401 response, so the mock arguably matches the spec as written. The residual value (exercising FE 401 paths in dev) is a nice-to-have. Downgrade to low; the requireUser helper proposal is fine if pursued.

title: Mock API has zero latency and (except validation) never fails, so loading/error states go unexercised
description: Every route handler responds synchronously from memory — there is no artificial delay or random failure anywhere (see e.g. app/api/contacts/route.ts:4-6, app/api/device/route.ts:4-6; the only nondeterminism is the 10% sample-failure at app/api/voice-training/samples/route.ts:31). The mock exists per requirements.md §5 'for FE development before real BE is ready', but with ~0ms responses the app's spinners (e.g. app/dashboard/contacts/page.tsx:50 `if (!channels) return <Spinner />`), busy states, and HTTP-error rendering are effectively invisible/untested during development, and latency-dependent bugs (double-submit, race between connect and list refresh) cannot surface.
