title: 2xx responses with empty/non-JSON bodies silently resolve to null typed as T
description: api() does `data = await res.json()` inside a try/catch that swallows parse failures (lib/api.ts:34-39), then `return data as T` (line 45). For an OK response whose body is empty (204 No Content — common for disconnect/delete on real backends) or non-JSON (proxy returning HTML with 200), the promise resolves with null while the caller's type says Channel[]/VoiceSample/etc. Consumers then misbehave silently: app/dashboard/contacts/page.tsx sets channels to null via `.then(setChannels)` and line 50's `if (!channels) return <Spinner />` shows an infinite spinner. Latent with the current mock (all handlers return JSON) but a trap for the intended real-BE swap.
proposal: Distinguish 'no body' from 'parse error on expected JSON': if res.status === 204 or Content-Length is 0, return undefined as T explicitly; otherwise, if JSON parsing fails on an ok response, throw new ApiError(res.status, 'Invalid response body') instead of resolving null.
verifierNote: Verified at lib/api.ts:34-39: res.json() failure is swallowed leaving data=null, and line 45 `return data as T` resolves null on any ok-but-bodyless response (204 etc.). Consumer impact checks out: app/dashboard/contacts/page.tsx:19 `.then(setChannels)` with null keeps the `if (!channels) return <Spinner />` branch at line 51 forever. Latent with the mock (all handlers return JSON bodies) but a real trap for the documented real-BE swap where 204 on disconnect is common. Low severity and the 204/parse-error distinction proposal are both right.

title: Fragile base-URL joining: trailing slash produces double slash, and the /api prefix is hardcoded in transport
description: The URL is built as `${BASE}/api${path}` (lib/api.ts:33) with BASE read raw from NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL (line 1). If the env var is set with a trailing slash (`https://api.example.com/`) requests go to `https://api.example.com//api/...`; some backends/proxies 404 or redirect on double slashes. Also, the `/api` path prefix lives in the transport layer, while README ('BE communication' section) claims lib/be.ts is 'the only place endpoints are defined' and the swap to a real BE needs edits 'in lib/be.ts (and lib/types.ts) only' — a real BE not mounted under /api would force an api.ts edit, contradicting the documented swap procedure.
proposal: Normalize once at module load: `const BASE = (process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL || "").replace(/\/+$/, "")`. Either move the '/api' prefix into be.ts paths, or document in README that the real BE must serve under /api (which requirements.md §5 line 43 does state as the base path).
verifierNote: Accurate: lib/api.ts:1 reads NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL raw, lib/api.ts:33 builds `${BASE}/api${path}` — a trailing-slash env value yields `//api/...`. And the `/api` prefix does live in transport while README.md:36 claims be.ts is 'the only place endpoints are defined' and README.md:45 says the swap needs edits in be.ts/types.ts only — a real BE not under /api contradicts that. requirements.md:43 does declare /api as the base path, so documenting that constraint (or normalizing BASE) is the right low-effort fix. Low confirmed.

title: No timeout or AbortSignal support in the transport layer or be.ts services
description: api() (lib/api.ts:21-33) sets no timeout and none of the be.ts service functions accept an AbortSignal (e.g. VoiceAPI.submitSample at lib/be.ts:68-76, LogsAPI.list at lib/be.ts:86-91). A hung request against a real backend leaves buttons stuck in their busy state forever (sign-in busy flag at app/sign-in/page.tsx:16-27 is only reset in catch/finally), and the voice-training page's polling of samples (app/dashboard/voice-training/page.tsx:42) cannot cancel in-flight requests on unmount, allowing state updates after navigation. Technically callers could smuggle a signal via the RequestInit spread, but no service function exposes it, and README declares pages must never call api()/fetch directly.
proposal: Add a default timeout in api() via `AbortSignal.timeout(15000)` (combine with any caller-provided signal via AbortSignal.any), map the resulting AbortError to ApiError(0, 'timeout'), and thread an optional `signal?: AbortSignal` parameter through the be.ts list/poll functions used by pollers.
verifierNote: Accurate: api() (lib/api.ts:21-33) sets no signal/timeout, and no be.ts function threads one (lib/be.ts:63-77 VoiceAPI, 85-92 LogsAPI). A hung request leaves sign-in busy forever (app/sign-in/page.tsx:21-27 — busy only resets in the catch branch), and the voice-training poller (app/dashboard/voice-training/page.tsx:41-45 setInterval on loadSamples) cannot abort in-flight requests on unmount. Callers could technically pass a signal via the RequestInit spread but be.ts (the mandated entry point per lib/be.ts:6-7) exposes none. Low is right — irrelevant against the same-origin mock, real only post-swap. AbortSignal.timeout proposal is sound.

title: Mock token embeds the role and is fully client-forgeable; token stored in localStorage
description: The mock token is unsigned base64url(JSON of the whole User) (lib/mock/token.ts:4-6) and decodeToken trusts whatever it decodes, validating only that id and email exist — not that role is a legal value (lib/mock/token.ts:8-19). Anyone can mint `base64url({id:'x',email:'x@x',role:'developer'})` in the console and read the developer-gated /api/logs (app/api/logs/route.ts:10-12). The token also lives in localStorage (lib/api.ts:3-11), readable by any XSS payload. Both are acknowledged as mock-only (lib/mock/token.ts:1, README 'Notes'), so this is a documentation/pattern concern rather than a live vulnerability — but the FE architecture (Bearer-from-localStorage) will carry straight over to the real BE per the swap plan.
proposal: Keep the mock as-is but add a note in README's 'Swapping mock → real backend' section that the real BE must use signed, expiring tokens and that httpOnly SameSite cookies (with the api() Authorization header injection removed) are preferred over localStorage Bearer tokens; have decodeToken at least whitelist role to 'user'|'developer' so forged roles outside the enum can't flow into the UI.
verifierNote: All facts verified: token is unsigned base64url(JSON(User)) (lib/mock/token.ts:4-6); decodeToken validates only id and email, not role (lib/mock/token.ts:14) — a console-forged developer token passes app/api/logs/route.ts:10-12's role gate; token lives in localStorage (lib/api.ts:3-11). The finding itself correctly frames this as acknowledged mock-only (lib/mock/token.ts:1, README.md:61) and proposes only documentation plus a role whitelist, which is proportionate. Low confirmed.

title: Weak input validation in mock handlers: non-numeric logs limit yields empty result; samples POST accepts unknown promptId
description: app/api/logs/route.ts:16 does `Number(url.searchParams.get("limit") || 50)`: `?limit=abc` → NaN → `logs.slice(0, NaN)` returns [] (silently empty list instead of a 400 or the default), `?limit=0` → 0 (string "0" is truthy so the || default doesn't apply) and negative limits slice from the array end. Separately, app/api/voice-training/samples/route.ts:16 validates only that promptId is a string — a promptId not present in PROMPTS (lib/mock/store.ts:89-115) is accepted and stored, producing history entries whose prompt text can't be resolved by the FE. Low impact because the shipped FE always sends well-formed values, but the mock is the executable contract for the future BE.
proposal: In the logs handler: `const limit = Math.min(Math.max(Number.parseInt(raw ?? "", 10) || 50, 1), 500)`. In the samples POST: reject promptIds not found in PROMPTS with 400, matching how connect validates against credentialFields.
verifierNote: Verified: app/api/logs/route.ts:16 `Number(url.searchParams.get("limit") || 50)` — '?limit=abc' → NaN → `logs.slice(0, NaN)` (line 25) → [] (NaN end coerces to 0); '?limit=0' → string "0" is truthy so the default is skipped → empty; negative limits slice from the end. And app/api/voice-training/samples/route.ts:16 only checks `typeof promptId !== "string"`, so unknown promptIds are stored; the FE falls back to rendering the raw id (app/dashboard/voice-training/page.tsx:198). Low is correctly calibrated (shipped FE always sends valid values via lib/be.ts:86-91); clamping proposal is sound.

But the seed data (lib/mock/store.ts:16-35) sets no error on any channel, and the only code touching the field clears it (app/api/contacts/[id]/connect/route.ts:24 `channel.error = null`); nothing ever sets a non-null error. The error branch of the Contacts UI is therefore unreachable against the mock and cannot be demoed or manually tested.

title: Deep links are lost through the sign-in redirect — user always lands on /dashboard/contacts
description: app/dashboard/layout.tsx:30-32 redirects unauthenticated visitors with `router.replace("/sign-in")`, discarding the requested pathname. After authentication, signIn/signUp hardcode `router.push("/dashboard")` (lib/auth.tsx:45,52), which app/dashboard/page.tsx:4 forwards to /dashboard/contacts. So a user opening a shared or bookmarked link like /dashboard/device or /dashboard/logs while signed out is dumped on the Contacts tab after signing in and must re-navigate manually. The audit lens and common expectation is that the original destination is preserved.
proposal: In the dashboard layout guard, redirect with the intended path: `router.replace(`/sign-in?next=${encodeURIComponent(pathname)}`)` (usePathname is already imported there). In the sign-in/sign-up pages, read the `next` search param, validate it starts with "/" (reject external URLs), and pass it to signIn/signUp so they `router.replace(next ?? "/dashboard")`.
verifierNote: Premise verified: app/dashboard/layout.tsx:31 `router.replace("/sign-in")` discards pathname; lib/auth.tsx:45,52 hardcode push("/dashboard"); app/dashboard/page.tsx:4 redirects to /dashboard/contacts. So deep links are indeed lost. But in this 4-tab mock-backed app the cost is one extra click on an in-app nav, and there is no external link-sharing surface (no emails, no notifications) that generates deep links today. Nice standard practice, low value at this maturity — downgrade to low. Proposal (validated `next` param) is otherwise correct.

title: Sign-up validation feedback is submit-only via a top banner instead of inline field errors
description: app/sign-up/page.tsx:22-29 checks password length and confirm-password mismatch only inside onSubmit, and renders the result as a single Alert banner above the form (line 42) rather than attached to the offending field. The Input primitive already supports an `error` prop with red border + message (components/ui.tsx:58-65), but no auth page uses it. The password input also lacks minLength={6}, so the browser gives no early hint either. A user only discovers 'Mật khẩu không khớp' after filling all three fields and pressing submit, then has to figure out which field is wrong; the stale banner also persists while they retype until the next submit.
proposal: Validate inline: track a confirm-field error computed when both password fields are non-empty (on change or on blur of confirm) and pass it as `error` to the confirm Input; similarly show the length error under the password field (and add minLength={6}). Keep the submit-time check as a backstop, and clear field errors as the user corrects them.
verifierNote: Facts correct: validation only in onSubmit (app/sign-up/page.tsx:22-29), single top Alert (line 42), Input supports an error prop with red border + message (components/ui.tsx:60,65) that no auth page uses, and the password input (app/sign-up/page.tsx:51-58) has no minLength (grep shows minLength only in app/dashboard/device/page.tsx:181). But this is polish, not a defect: the messages are localized (t("passwordMismatch")), appear instantly on submit without a network round-trip, and the form has only 3 fields. Inline errors + minLength are worth doing but low value — downgrade medium→low.

title: No password visibility toggle on any of the three password fields

The product's stated audience is seniors (tagline 'Người bạn đồng hành AI cho người lớn tuổi', lib/i18n.tsx:10), a group with elevated typo rates in masked fields; combined with sign-up requiring the password twice and errors only appearing on submit, this causes avoidable failed submissions. lucide-react (already a dependency, used in app/dashboard/layout.tsx:6) ships Eye/EyeOff icons.

Use it for all three password fields; on sign-up, one toggle per field (or a single toggle for both new-password fields).

title: Forgot-password is a dead end — no reset-password route exists to complete the flow
description: requirements.md:14 requires 'Forgot/reset password (own route)'. Today /forgot-password posts the email (app/forgot-password/page.tsx:22), the mock unconditionally returns { ok: true } (app/api/auth/forgot-password/route.ts:8-9), and the page shows 'Nếu email tồn tại, liên kết đặt lại đã được gửi' with a back-to-sign-in link (app/forgot-password/page.tsx:33-42). But no /reset-password page or POST /api/auth/reset-password mock exists anywhere (app/ has only sign-in, sign-up, forgot-password, dashboard), so the 'reset' half of the requirement cannot be demonstrated end-to-end, and the FE pattern for the real BE's reset link landing page is unbuilt. Note the forgot-password endpoint itself is also absent from the requirements §5 API contract (requirements.md:45-60).

On success, show a success alert linking to /sign-in. If deliberately out of scope for the mock phase, at minimum state on the sent-confirmation screen that reset completion is pending backend support.

title: Authenticated users still see the sign-in/sign-up forms; post-login push() makes Back return to the form
description: Neither app/sign-in/page.tsx nor app/sign-up/page.tsx checks `user` from useAuth — a signed-in user navigating to /sign-in (bookmark, back button) gets a live credentials form instead of being forwarded to the dashboard. Compounding this, signIn/signUp use `router.push("/dashboard")` (lib/auth.tsx:45,52), so immediately after logging in, one press of Back lands on the sign-in form while still authenticated — a confusing loop-feeling flow (app/page.tsx:14 uses replace() correctly for the same reason).
proposal: In the auth pages (or a shared (auth) route-group layout), when `!loading && user` redirect to /dashboard with router.replace. Change router.push to router.replace in signIn/signUp so the auth form is not in the back-stack after a successful login.

Low severity and the replace + redirect-if-user proposal are both correct.

title: Stale me() response can clobber a fresh login token (race in AuthProvider)
description: AuthProvider fires AuthAPI.me() on mount when a token exists (lib/auth.tsx:29-39) with no cancellation or staleness check. If that token is invalid and the request is slow (throttled network), the user can reach /sign-in and submit before it settles; signIn stores the NEW token (lib/auth.tsx:43), then the old me() call rejects with 401 and its `.catch(() => setToken(null))` deletes the new token from localStorage. The user appears signed in (user state was set) but every subsequent request goes out without an Authorization header — with a real BE, all dashboard data 401s until re-login.
proposal: Guard the callback against staleness: capture the token used for the request and inside catch only call setToken(null) if `getToken() === token` (i.e., it hasn't been replaced). An AbortController or an `active` flag in the effect cleanup would equally solve it.
verifierNote: Verified race: the mount effect (lib/auth.tsx:29-39) has no cleanup/staleness guard; the sign-in page renders its form regardless of `loading` (app/sign-in/page.tsx has no loading gate), so a user at /sign-in can submit while a slow me() with a stale invalid token is in flight; signIn stores the new token (lib/auth.tsx:43), then the old me()'s 401 rejection runs `.catch(() => setToken(null))` (line 37) and deletes the NEW token — user state stays set (line 44) so the UI looks signed in while every api() call goes out headerless (lib/api.ts:28-29). Narrow preconditions justify low; the getToken()===token guard proposal is minimal and correct.

title: Sign-out and sign-in are not synchronized across tabs
description: The token lives in localStorage (lib/api.ts:3-11), which is shared across tabs, but AuthProvider only reads it once on mount (lib/auth.tsx:29-39) and signOut (lib/auth.tsx:55-59) updates React state in the current tab only. Signing out in tab A leaves tab B fully operational with the in-memory user; conversely a 401-triggered token wipe in one tab leaves other tabs sending requests with a header from a now-removed token until reload. No `storage` event listener exists anywhere in lib/ or app/.
proposal: In AuthProvider, add a window `storage` event listener for the "token" key: on removal, setUser(null) (the dashboard layout guard then redirects); on a new value, re-run AuthAPI.me() to hydrate the user. Remove the listener in the effect cleanup.
verifierNote: Main premise holds: no `storage` (or any) event listener exists in lib/app/components (grep for addEventListener returns nothing), token lives in localStorage (lib/api.ts:3-11), and signOut only mutates current-tab React state (lib/auth.tsx:55-59), so tab B keeps its in-memory user and rendered dashboard. But one sub-claim is factually wrong: other tabs would NOT keep 'sending requests with a header from a now-removed token' — api() calls getToken() fresh from localStorage on every request (lib/api.ts:28-29), so after a wipe, tab B's requests go out with no Authorization header and 401 (then get swallowed per finding 0). Severity low is right; keep the proposal but correct the failure description.

title: Bearer token persisted in localStorage — XSS-readable, no expiry; pattern will carry over to the real backend
description: getToken/setToken use localStorage (lib/api.ts:3-11) and api() injects it as an Authorization header (lib/api.ts:28-29). localStorage is synchronously readable by any injected script, and the token has no client-side expiry handling. For the current same-origin mock this is acknowledged debt (README.md:61 'Mock token is base64 JSON — not secure, mock only'), but lib/api.ts is the permanent transport layer that stays when NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL points at the real backend (requirements.md:137), so the storage decision silently ships to production.
proposal: Document the intended production auth transport now and design lib/api.ts for it: prefer an httpOnly SameSite cookie session (api() adds credentials: "include" and drops the header) or, if Bearer is mandated, keep the access token in memory with a refresh flow rather than localStorage. At minimum add a code comment in lib/api.ts marking the storage choice as mock-phase-only so the BE swap revisits it.
verifierNote: Facts verified: localStorage get/set at lib/api.ts:3-11, Bearer header injection at lib/api.ts:28-29, no expiry handling anywhere; README.md:61 acknowledges the mock token only ('Mock token is base64 JSON — not secure, mock only') and lib/mock/token.ts:1 comments on the FORMAT, not the storage choice — lib/api.ts itself carries no such marker and is the transport that survives the NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL swap (requirements.md §6). As a low-severity advisory with a minimal proposal (document the decision / plan cookie-or-in-memory transport), it is accurate and proportionate.

title: No success feedback after connecting a channel

Failure gets an explicit in-modal Alert (page.tsx:92) but success gets nothing, which is asymmetric — the lens requirement is feedback for both outcomes, and other tabs already show explicit success messages (e.g. 'wifiUpdated'/'submitted' keys in lib/i18n.tsx:86,61).

The final layout is a predictable 2-column grid of fixed-shape cards, which is the ideal case for skeletons.

title: Voice-sample polling runs forever in hidden/background tabs
description: The 5-second setInterval poll (lines 41-45) keeps firing while the tab is hidden or the laptop lid produces throttled timers, hammering GET /voice-training/samples indefinitely — and since the mock's setTimeout status transition dies on serverless (already flagged), 'pending' can persist forever, making this an unbounded request loop. No reviewer flagged the visibility dimension. The same applies to any future device-status polling requirements §7 anticipates.
proposal: Gate the interval on document.visibilityState (pause on 'hidden', refetch once on 'visible' via a visibilitychange listener), and add a max-poll-duration or backoff so a permanently-pending sample cannot poll forever.
verifierNote: Verified: voice-training/page.tsx:41-45 sets a 5s setInterval whenever any sample is pending, with no visibilitychange/visibilityState gating and no max duration or backoff. The permanently-pending scenario is grounded: the mock flips status via an in-request setTimeout (app/api/voice-training/samples/route.ts:30-32) that dies on serverless, so the pending predicate at line 42 can stay true forever and the interval re-arms on every poll result. Browsers do throttle hidden-tab intervals (so 'hammering' is tempered), which the finding itself acknowledges — low severity is correctly calibrated and the fix is proportionate.

title: No security headers configured despite localStorage tokens and pasted channel secrets
description: next.config.ts:3 is an empty object — no headers() defining Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy. The app stores a bearer token in XSS-readable localStorage (flagged separately) and users paste channel access tokens (Zalo/Messenger/Telegram secrets) into forms; the missing CSP is the second half of that risk since any injected script exfiltrates both. A Permissions-Policy is also relevant here because the app legitimately uses the microphone and should scope it to self.
proposal: Add an async headers() block in next.config.ts applying a baseline CSP (default-src 'self' plus what Next needs), frame-ancestors 'none', Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin, and Permissions-Policy: microphone=(self). This is independent of the mock backend and carries over to production unchanged.
verifierNote: Verified: next.config.ts:3 is `const nextConfig: NextConfig = {};` — no headers() and no middleware.ts exists. The token lives in localStorage (lib/api.ts:3-11) and the contacts modal collects channel secrets like accessToken/pageAccessToken in plain inputs (app/dashboard/contacts/page.tsx:94-102, field names from requirements.md:66-67). Permissions-Policy: microphone=(self) is apt given the getUserMedia use (voice-training/page.tsx:61). Low is the right severity — CSP for Next.js needs nonce/'unsafe-inline' tuning so 'carries over unchanged' is slightly optimistic, but the proposal is directionally sound and independent of the mock.

title: Sign-in page permanently ships a hint that teaches users how to self-escalate to developer role
description: app/sign-in/page.tsx:67 renders t("signInHint") — 'Tip (mock): emails containing "dev" get the developer role' (lib/i18n.tsx:27,121) — as a permanent dictionary string with no env gating. Combined with roleForEmail (lib/mock/token.ts:21-23), any visitor can mint a developer account and open the role-gated Logs tab. Reviewers flagged the forgeable token, but not that the production sign-in UI itself documents the escalation recipe; because the string lives in the permanent i18n dictionary rather than behind a mock flag, it will still render after NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL is pointed at the real backend.

There is no env gating anywhere, and since the mock-vs-real switch is only NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL (lib/api.ts:1, requirements.md:137), the hint would indeed survive pointing at the real backend. Low severity and the env-gating proposal are appropriate.

title: Mock sign-in mints a brand-new random user id on every login and validates against no user store
description: app/api/auth/sign-in/route.ts:12-16 creates `id: u_<random>` per request and never consults the store — sign-up (app/api/auth/sign-up/route.ts) likewise persists nothing, so 'accounts' don't exist: the documented 401 'Invalid credentials' path is unreachable except via password.length < 6, and the same person gets a different user.id every session. Any FE logic keyed on user.id (per-user sample history, preferences — natural next features) would silently break across logins, and the invalid-credentials UX on the sign-in page can never be exercised against the mock. Adjacent findings covered 'mock never fails' latency-wise, but not the unstable identity or the unreachable 401 contract path.
proposal: Derive the id deterministically from the email (e.g. `u_` + base64url(email)) in both sign-in and sign-up, and add one hardcoded rejection case (e.g. password 'wrongpass' → 401) so the sign-in error path is actually testable, mirroring the §5 contract.
verifierNote: Verified: app/api/auth/sign-in/route.ts:12-16 mints `u_${Math.random()...}` per request and consults no store; app/api/auth/sign-up/route.ts:15-20 does the same and persists nothing (lib/mock/store.ts is never touched by auth routes). The 401 at sign-in lines 6-11 fires only for missing fields or password.length < 6 — and the form's `required` inputs (app/sign-in/page.tsx:39,47) make short-password the only reachable path, so the requirements.md:55 'Invalid credentials' contract is effectively untestable and identity is unstable across sessions. Impact today is nil (no mock data is keyed on user.id), which the 'low' severity correctly reflects; the deterministic-id proposal is minimal and sound.

title: Correction: design-system 'no focus-visible styles in ANY primitive' is overstated for Input and the logs select
description: The design-system/high finding claims no primitive has focus styles and that the logs select 'removes the outline entirely'. In fact Input (components/ui.tsx:59) applies `focus:border-sen focus:ring-2 focus:ring-sen-light` — a clearly visible focus indicator — and the logs select (app/dashboard/logs/page.tsx:38) pairs its `outline-none` with `focus:border-sen`, a weak but present indicator. The real, defensible gap is Button (ui.tsx:26), the modal backdrop/buttons, nav Links (dashboard/layout.tsx:78), the expandable log-row button (logs/page.tsx:85), and LanguageSwitcher buttons — all with zero focus styling. Fixing per the original wording risks 'adding' focus styles to Input that already exist while under-scoping the button/link work.

And the rescoped gap list is real: Button base classes (ui.tsx:26) have zero focus styles across all four variants (16-22), nav Links (dashboard/layout.tsx:77-82) have none, the log-row expander button (logs/page.tsx:85) has none, LanguageSwitcher buttons (components/LanguageSwitcher.tsx:13-17) have none, and the sign-out icon button (dashboard/layout.tsx:64) has none. title: Brand tokens duplicated as hex literals; two different 'success greens' coexist
description: The @theme palette (app/globals.css:4-15) is the single source of truth, but components/Logo.tsx:16-51 hardcodes the same values as hex literals (stroke="#2f6bb3" duplicates --color-sen, #5ea53c duplicates --color-leaf, #c9a24b duplicates --color-gold), and globals.css:24 hardcodes body color #1e293b. Status colors bypass the brand palette entirely: Badge success is Tailwind green-100/700 (components/ui.tsx:97) while the device page's signal bars use brand `bg-leaf` (app/dashboard/device/page.tsx:125) — two visibly different greens meaning 'good' on the same screen. A brand-color change would silently desync the logo, and status semantics have no tokens.
proposal: Reference CSS vars in the inline SVG (fill="var(--color-sen)" etc. — valid in inline SVG), replace body color with a token, and add semantic status tokens (--color-success/-warning/-danger + soft variants) in @theme mapped once, consumed by Badge, Alert, and the signal bars. Also delete or use the unused LogoWordmark export (Logo.tsx:56-60).

Badge green is Tailwind green-100/700 (ui.tsx:97) while signal bars are bg-leaf (#5ea53c, device/page.tsx:125) — both appear on the device screen (component-health badges at device/page.tsx:152 alongside the bars). title: Spinner is one-size with a baked-in layout wrapper; doubles as an uncentered full-page loader
description: Spinner (components/ui.tsx:163-169) hardcodes a `flex justify-center py-10` wrapper and an 8x8 circle, yet is used for three very different jobs: full-viewport route gates (app/page.tsx:17, app/dashboard/layout.tsx:34 — where it renders as a small circle near the top of an otherwise blank cream screen, not vertically centered, with no branding), section loading (voice-training/page.tsx:187, logs/page.tsx:75), and it cannot be used inline (e.g. inside the loading Button proposed above). There are also no skeleton primitives, so every tab paints a spinner then layout-shifts to full content.

Used as full-route gate at app/page.tsx:17 and dashboard/layout.tsx:34 (also contacts/page.tsx:51, device/page.tsx:59, logs/page.tsx:35) — with only py-10 and no min-h-screen it sits near the top of a blank page, not vertically centered. title: No dark-mode strategy and no color-scheme declaration for native controls
description: There are zero `dark:` variants in the codebase (verified by grep across app/ and components/) and all primitives hardcode light surfaces (bg-white in Card ui.tsx:80, Modal ui.tsx:153, header layout.tsx:40). Shipping light-only is a legitimate choice, but globals.css never declares `color-scheme`, so on a dark-OS device the browser may render native widgets — the logs <select> (logs/page.tsx:48), the <audio controls> player in voice training (voice-training/page.tsx:173), scrollbars — with dark UA styling inside an otherwise light page, a jarring mismatch precisely on the two most control-heavy screens.
proposal: Minimum: add `:root { color-scheme: light; }` to globals.css to force consistent native-control rendering. If dark mode is ever wanted, the @theme token layer is already the right seam — define surface/text semantic tokens now (--surface, --text-primary) so primitives stop hardcoding bg-white/slate literals.
verifierNote: Facts verified: zero dark: variants (grep matches only token names --color-sen-dark/--color-lotus-dark), no color-scheme declaration anywhere, bg-white hardcoded in Card (ui.tsx:80), Modal (ui.tsx:153), header (dashboard/layout.tsx:40), native select at logs/page.tsx:48 and <audio controls> at voice-training/page.tsx:173. But the premise is overstated: per spec, with no color-scheme declared the UA renders form controls light ('normal' scheme) even on a dark OS — the dark-widget mismatch only arises under browser forced/auto dark modes, where plain `color-scheme: light` is not the opt-out (`color-scheme: only light` / meta color-scheme is). Keep at low; the one-line addition is harmless hygiene but the stated failure mode mostly doesn't occur as described.

title: Timestamps formatted with browser locale, ignoring the app's selected language
description: Both timestamp render sites use no-argument `new Date(...).toLocaleString()` — sample history at app/dashboard/voice-training/page.tsx:201 and the logs list at app/dashboard/logs/page.tsx:103. The no-arg form uses the browser's OS/browser locale, not the app language from useI18n, so a user on an en-US browser who switched the app to Vietnamese still sees '7/9/2026, 10:00:00 AM' (and vice versa: vi-VN browsers show '10:00:00 9/7/2026' under the English UI). The format also does not change when the user toggles the language switcher, unlike every other string on the page. Both components already have `lang` available in scope (voice page destructures it at line 13; logs page can).
proposal: Pass the app locale explicitly: `new Date(s.createdAt).toLocaleString(lang === 'vi' ? 'vi-VN' : 'en-US')` at both sites, or better, expose a memoized `Intl.DateTimeFormat` (e.g. a formatDate helper on the i18n context in lib/i18n.tsx) so all future date rendering follows the selected language consistently.
verifierNote: Both sites verified: app/dashboard/voice-training/page.tsx:201 `new Date(s.createdAt).toLocaleString()` and app/dashboard/logs/page.tsx:103 `new Date(log.timestamp).toLocaleString()` — no locale argument, so browser locale wins over app language. Voice page already destructures lang at page.tsx:13. Low severity and the explicit-locale fix are appropriate.

title: Page metadata (browser tab title/description) is Vietnamese-only regardless of language
description: app/layout.tsx:5-9 exports a static Metadata object with a Vietnamese-only title ('SEN — Người bạn đồng hành AI') and description. No route segment overrides it and nothing updates document.title on language switch, so English users always see a Vietnamese browser-tab title, bookmark name, and share preview. The tagline translation already exists in the dictionary (lib/i18n.tsx:10,105) but is unused for metadata.

If cookie-based language persistence is adopted (see related finding), generate metadata server-side per saved language via generateMetadata reading the cookie, which also localizes the description for SEO/share cards.

title: Role badge shows raw role string; dict 'developer'/'user' keys are untranslated and dead
description: The header badge renders `{user.role}` directly (app/dashboard/layout.tsx:57-59), bypassing t(). The dictionary does define developer/user keys, but their Vietnamese values are the English words themselves — developer: 'developer', user: 'user' (lib/i18n.tsx:95-96) — and grep confirms t('developer')/t('user') are never called anywhere, so the keys are simultaneously dead code and untranslated. Vietnamese users see an English 'user'/'developer' chip in the header on every dashboard page. Additionally the 'time' and 'language' dict keys (lib/i18n.tsx:70,94) are defined but never referenced.

title: Brand/aria strings hardcoded outside the dictionary: English 'SEN logo' aria-label, literal 'SEN', raw 'SSID' label

title: No refresh or auto-refresh on the Logs tab
description: Logs are fetched only on mount and on filter change (app/dashboard/logs/page.tsx:27-33). There is no Refresh button (the Device tab has one at app/dashboard/device/page.tsx:72) and no auto-refresh, even though this tab exists to inspect live device↔backend traffic (requirements.md:33-35). To see new events a developer must toggle a filter back and forth or reload the page.

But the premise overstates the requirement — requirements.md:33-35 asks only for a filterable list with payload viewer, nothing about 'live' traffic; live-status mechanism is explicitly undecided (requirements.md:142). title: Hard 50-entry cap with no pagination, count, or load-more; malformed limit returns empty list
description: lib/be.ts:86 hardcodes `limit = 50` and no caller ever overrides it; app/api/logs/route.ts:25 does `logs.slice(0, limit)` with no offset/cursor. The UI (app/dashboard/logs/page.tsx) exposes no way to see beyond the first 50 entries and gives no indication that results are truncated — with a real backend, older logs are silently unreachable, compounding the missing time filter. Additionally, app/api/logs/route.ts:16 parses limit as `Number(url.searchParams.get("limit") || 50)`: `?limit=abc` yields NaN and `slice(0, NaN)` returns `[]`, so a malformed limit produces an empty 200 response instead of a default or 400.
proposal: Add `offset` (or cursor) support to the mock route and a "Load more" button (or limit selector 50/100/200) in the UI, plus a "showing N of M" count. In the route, clamp limit: `const n = Number(...); const limit = Number.isFinite(n) && n > 0 ? n : 50;`.
verifierNote: All facts verified: lib/be.ts:86 defaults limit=50 with no overriding caller; app/api/logs/route.ts:16 `Number(url.searchParams.get("limit") || 50)` yields NaN for ?limit=abc and line 25 slice(0, NaN) returns []. But the mock seeds only 40 logs (lib/mock/store.ts:50) so truncation never occurs today, and the client always sends limit=50 (lib/be.ts:87) so the NaN path requires a hand-crafted request against a throwaway mock. Real pagination is speculative until the real BE contract lands (requirements.md:141). The one-line clamp is worth doing; overall value is low, not medium.

title: Device status never updates live — single fetch on mount, no polling or freshness indicator
description: The device page fetches once on mount (`useEffect(load, [load])`, app/dashboard/device/page.tsx:39) and thereafter only on manual Refresh. requirements.md:142 explicitly designed the mock GET /api/device to be polling-friendly for live device status. Today, a component going offline or signal degrading is never reflected unless the user thinks to click Refresh, and there is no "last updated" indicator, so users cannot tell how stale the health/signal data is — a real problem for a monitoring surface aimed at an elderly-care device.
proposal: Add interval polling (e.g. every 10-15s): setInterval calling load() in a useEffect with cleanup on unmount, skipping ticks when `document.hidden` (or pausing via visibilitychange listener). Show a small "last updated: HH:mm:ss" caption near the Refresh button, updated on each successful load.
verifierNote: Premise accurate: single fetch on mount (app/dashboard/device/page.tsx:39) plus manual Refresh only, no last-updated indicator. But requirements.md:142 explicitly says WebSocket/SSE vs polling is 'not yet decided' — polling is deliberately an open product decision, not a gap the FE was supposed to close. The 'last updated' caption is a cheap genuine improvement; auto-polling is premature. Downgrade to low.

title: Device API routes have no auth guard, unlike /api/logs
description: GET /api/device (app/api/device/route.ts:4-6) and POST /api/device/wifi (app/api/device/wifi/route.ts:4-16) perform no token check at all, while /api/logs correctly decodes the Bearer token and returns 401/403 (app/api/logs/route.ts:6-12). Any unauthenticated request can read the home network SSID/IP and rewrite the device's Wi-Fi config. It is a mock, but the client always sends the token (lib/api.ts:28-29), the mock is the reference contract for the real BE (requirements.md:141), and the inconsistency between routes makes the intended auth surface ambiguous.
proposal: Add the same guard used in app/api/logs/route.ts to both device routes: `const user = decodeToken(req.headers.get("authorization")); if (!user) return NextResponse.json({ error: "Unauthorized" }, { status: 401 });`.
verifierNote: Facts about the cited routes are correct: app/api/device/route.ts:4-6 and app/api/device/wifi/route.ts:4-16 have no decodeToken guard while app/api/logs/route.ts:6-12 does. But the framing of inconsistency is misleading: grep shows decodeToken is used only in /api/auth/me and /api/logs; /api/contacts and /api/voice-training routes are also unauthenticated (app/api/contacts/route.ts:4-6, app/api/voice-training/samples/route.ts:5-10). The mock's evident pattern is: auth check only where role gating matters (logs). This is an in-process mock with fake data, so there is no real exposure; the 'reference contract' argument has some merit but requirements.md:141 says the mock is a placeholder. Adding guards is fine but low value — not medium/security.

title: Payload viewer lacks copy-to-clipboard and vertical bounding for large payloads
description: The payload/response panes (app/dashboard/logs/page.tsx:112-123) pretty-print JSON into <pre> blocks with only `overflow-x-auto` — there is no copy button (a developer wanting to replay or diff a payload must manually select text inside a dark <pre>), and no max-height, so a real-world multi-KB payload will stretch the card to an enormous height, pushing all subsequent log rows off screen.

Mock payloads are small (lib/mock/store.ts:61-66) but real payloads won't be. Low severity is correctly calibrated; proposal is proportionate.

title: Wi-Fi failure shows raw English server error and validation is opaque
description: On failure the modal renders `err.message` directly (app/dashboard/device/page.tsx:53), which for the mock is always the English string "Failed to connect" (app/api/device/wifi/route.ts:7) regardless of the app language (vi is the default). The server also collapses distinct causes — empty SSID, password under 8 chars, actual connect failure — into that one generic message, and the form gives no hint about the 8-character minimum until native validation blocks submit (minLength at line 181).

title: Wi-Fi password field has no show/hide toggle
description: The Wi-Fi password input is a plain `type="password"` field (app/dashboard/device/page.tsx:175-182) with no reveal toggle. Wi-Fi passphrases are typically long random strings; a masked-only field makes typos likely, and a typo here is costly — the ESP32 device drops off the network and the elderly end-user loses the assistant until someone re-fixes it. Standard practice for network-credential entry (routers, phone OS Wi-Fi dialogs) is a show-password affordance.
proposal: Add an eye/eye-off toggle button (lucide Eye/EyeOff) inside or beside the input that switches the type between "password" and "text", since this is a one-time entry dialog rather than a login form.
verifierNote: Verified: app/dashboard/device/page.tsx:175-182 is a plain type="password" Input with no reveal toggle; lucide-react is already a dependency (imported at line 4). Reasonable low-severity UX improvement for one-time network-credential entry.

title: Wi-Fi success banner persists indefinitely and is never reset
description: After a successful Wi-Fi change, `setUpdated(true)` (app/dashboard/device/page.tsx:48) shows the success Alert (lines 77-81), but `updated` is never set back to false — no timeout, no dismiss control, and it is not cleared when the user opens the modal again. The "Connected to new Wi-Fi!" banner therefore stays for the life of the page, and if a subsequent change attempt fails, the stale success banner remains visible behind the modal, contradicting the error shown inside it.

So the success banner persists for the page lifetime and remains visible behind the modal during a subsequent failed attempt. Low is calibrated.

title: POST /api/auth/forgot-password exists in code but not in the §5 mock API contract
description: The §5 Auth contract (requirements.md:45-60) defines only sign-up, sign-in, and me. The implementation adds AuthAPI.forgotPassword calling POST /api/auth/forgot-password (lib/be.ts:41-45) with a matching mock handler (app/api/auth/forgot-password/route.ts). The endpoint is needed to satisfy §3's forgot-password requirement, but because it was never added to the contract, a real backend built strictly from §5 will not implement it and the deployed forgot-password page will 404 the moment NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL is switched to the real BE (§7 explicitly warns the real contract may differ). This is spec drift: code and contract have silently diverged.
proposal: Update requirements.md §5 Auth to document POST /api/auth/forgot-password { email } -> 200 { ok: true } (and the reset endpoint if added per the reset-flow finding), so the real BE team implements it. Alternatively, if the BE will use a different path, adjust lib/be.ts now — it is the designated single point of change per its own header comment.

AuthAPI.forgotPassword posts to /auth/forgot-password (lib/be.ts:41-45) with a mock handler at app/api/auth/forgot-password/route.ts. requirements.md:141 (§7) confirms the real BE contract is built from this spec, so the drift is real: a BE implementing §5 strictly omits the endpoint and the deployed forgot-password page breaks. Documentation-only fix, low severity is correct.

title: Device Config never auto-refreshes — 'monitor device health' is stale until manual refresh
description: §1 states the hub lets users "monitor device health", and §7 notes the mock GET /api/device is deliberately "polling-friendly" while the WS/SSE decision is open. Contrast with voice-training, which does auto-poll pending samples (voice-training/page.tsx:41-45). A user watching the Device tab will never see a component go offline/error or Wi-Fi signal change without manually clicking Refresh, which undercuts the monitoring goal and leaves §7's polling option unexercised.

Keeping the transport behind DeviceAPI.info() preserves the §7 flexibility to swap polling for WebSocket/SSE later without touching the page. Optionally show a 'last updated' timestamp next to the Refresh button.

title: Wi-Fi change flow requires an 8+ character password, making open networks unconfigurable
description: The §5 contract for POST /api/device/wifi (requirements.md:129-132) specifies body { ssid: string, password: string } with a 400 only for connection failure — it defines no minimum password length. title: Mock's setTimeout status transition dies on serverless — samples stay pending forever and the client polls indefinitely
